entity.appearance: Disguised (Disguise Self, until about 12:08): a lean, clean-shaven young bath attendant with cropped hair, a rose-embroidered linen tunic, wet sandals, a towel over one arm, and a folded hand towel and a brass linen-hook at his hip.

bio.appearance: Late twenties, lean and quick, ink-black hair cropped short, sharp jaw, restless grey eyes. Charcoal layers with a dozen hidden pockets. A silver magpie-feather pin worn inside his collar, the last gift from his mother. A thin white scar across his left palm from a bad lock at age twelve. He/him.
bio.backstory: Raised on the rooftops of the Tangle, Kit could climb before he could read and pick a lock before he could sign his name. The Magpie taught him everything except how to do the last job. The night she went after the Meridian she said, 'Back before the bells, little jackdaw.' The bells rang. She never came home. In the six years since, Kit has made a name as a second-story artist, running jobs for Crane and asking every fence in the city the same question. Tonight a whisper brought him to the Night Market, where one of the auction lots is listed as 'The Magpie's Key.'
bio.bonds: His mother Marisol Corvell, 'the Magpie', the greatest thief Vessarine ever knew, who vanished six years ago. 'Uncle Val' Crane, her old fence, who kept Kit fed after she was gone.
bio.flaws: Can't walk away from a lock nobody has picked or a mark nobody has beaten. Trusts old friends far too easily.
bio.goals: Find out what happened to his mother. Beat the building that beat her.
bio.ideals: Freedom. Nothing beautiful and no one living should be locked away. Rob the powerful, never the desperate.
bio.personality: Cool under pressure, warm with friends, allergic to being told something can't be done. Plans three moves ahead and improvises the fourth. Hides worry behind a crooked grin and terrible jokes.

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.name: Warden's Sigil Ring
inventory.source: stolen: pried off Sergeant Varga's chained hand in the Heron's brig

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: A folded order on the Meridian's cream letter-paper, sealed with the museum's orrery stamp: 'Pellow & Sons, Vintner's Row. inventory.name: Wine delivery order
inventory.source: stolen: coat pocket in Pell's cabinet 8, Rosewater Baths

Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: A folded order on the Meridian's cream letter-paper, sealed with the museum's orrery stamp: 'Pellow & Sons, Vintner's Row. Sixty (60) bottles, Sable Vine '31, for the Lantern Gala. Deliver the afternoon of the eighth day, third bell, to the SERVICE LANDING (east water-stairs). Present this order to the landing warden for admittance of the cart and one (1) porter. Signed, E. Marrow, Steward of the Household.'
inventory.name: Wine delivery order
inventory.source: stolen: coat pocket in Pell's cabinet 8, Rosewater Baths

inventory.description: Five iron and brass keys on a ring with a cork tag reading PELLOW & SONS - VINTNER'S ROW. Front door, cellar, counting-room, and two smaller cabinet keys.

inventory.description: Lettie's iron ring of six keys: front doors, staff door, linen room, stoke-hole, till, and a small brass one unmarked.
inventory.name: Staff key-ring

inventory.description: A second-hand drover's coat of heavy brown frieze, patched at both elbows, smelling of horse and pipe smoke.
inventory.name: Drover's coat
inventory.source: gift: traded from Nance Pettle's rag stall, the Tanners' Cut, for the silver scent bottle

inventory.description: An unfinished letter in Ambrose Tull's big, cheerful hand to his broker Mr Oakes of Saltgate, about seized Emberleaf and his card for the Meridian's Gala. It breaks off unsigned, but it's a full page of his handwriting.

inventory.source: stolen: Ambrose Tull's writing-box, the Peony Suite

inventory.description: A cream page torn cleanly close to the spine of the Silver Ewer's guest register, listing a day's arrivals. Among them, in a big looping hand: 'Ambrose Tull, Saltgate, the Peony.'
inventory.name: Page from the Silver Ewer's guest register
inventory.source: stolen: the Silver Ewer's guest register

inventory.description: A ready-made gentleman's suit from Faircloth's of Silk Lane: close-cut charcoal worsted coat and waistcoat with dull horn buttons, white shirt, black silk stock, dark trousers, good black boots and a low-crowned black hat. Stylish, quiet, expensive-looking without shining.
inventory.name: Fine clothes (charcoal)
inventory.source: gift: bought by Asche at Faircloth's for 15 gp

inventory.description: A steel ring of keys: the Alcazar's stage door, the keeper's box, and a small cupboard key from the box.
inventory.name: Alcazar stage-door keys
inventory.source: loot: Mrs Danby's basket, Lamplight Mews

inventory.description: The key to Mrs Danby's two rooms over the Alcazar's carpentry shop, on a faded ribbon.
inventory.name: Mrs Danby's door key
inventory.source: loot: Mrs Danby's neck, Lamplight Mews

inventory.description: A cream envelope of heavy, old-fashioned paper, sealed in black wax stamped with a closed eye, the same mark as on Crane's black-gold coin.
inventory.name: Black-sealed envelope
inventory.source: gift: left for the crew under the blue lamp, the Blue Lamp, Gilder's Row

inventory.description: Three small brass keys on a steel neck-chain, one for each lock of Quill's iron strongbox.
inventory.name: Quill's strongbox keys

inventory.description: The big iron key to Quill's green door on Needle Row.
inventory.name: Quill's door key

inventory.description: A plain envelope marked NELL in a tiny, precise clerk's hand, left with Mother Ruddock by Pim Hobb.

inventory.name: Paper
inventory.note: About thirty blank customs clearance forms from before the Council's new quay, kept dry in an oilcloth wrap. Each is headed with the old harbour customs crest and has spaces for vessel, master, cargo, duty paid and the Collector's seal. Good stock for a forger.
inventory.source: found: oilcloth bundle in the clerks' pigeonholes, Old Customs House

inventory.name: Rapier
inventory.note: Valentin Crane's walking cane: black lacquered wood with a silver heron's-head handle. A twist of the handle draws a slim, needle-pointed blade. It passes for a gentleman's cane anywhere a sword would draw looks. The engine treats it as a Rapier.
inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.
inventory.name: Oilcloth wrap

inventory.description: Sergeant Mallory's Collector sigil: a heavy brass disc stamped with the sun-and-key, on a thick chain worn smooth by his collar. Warden-grade.
inventory.name: Collector's Brass Sigil
inventory.source: stolen: off the hook by the ledger desk while Mallory signed

inventory.description: A heavy black iron ring set with a gold sun-and-key, warm from the Grand Curator's glove. Her personal sigil: the only key that quiets the plate on her own door below Cage Four.
inventory.name: The Curator's Ring
inventory.source: stolen: tossed to Kit by the charmed Curator, Cage Four

inventory.description: A folded plan of the Rotunda for Gala night in the Curator's hand: concentric rings of seats under the great lens, guests' names in each. The innermost ring holds seven names, the seven Councillors of Vessarine, each marked with a tiny gold sun.
inventory.name: The Gala seating chart

inventory.description: A slim daybook bound in black calf, the Curator's tight hand on every page: appointments, acquisitions, and things she tells no one.
inventory.name: The Curator's daybook

inventory.description: A small, heavy brass key on a fine gold chain, worn warm under the Grand Curator's collar. Its bow is cast with a tiny sun-and-key.
inventory.name: Small brass key on a fine chain
inventory.source: loot: from round the Curator's neck, in her sanctum

inventory.description: The Curator's own Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame, a gold sun-and-key on the brow, a leather strap. Worn down, it turns the world to dusk.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor (gilded, sun-and-key)

inventory.description: A Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame with a leather strap.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor

inventory.description: An iron reliquary the size of a melon, shaped like a closed eye: two curved lids riveted with gold. Inside, the Ysmeran Eye. Cold, heavy, and patient. Do not open the lids without a visor.
inventory.name: The Ysmeran Eye (in its iron reliquary)
inventory.source: stolen: the Eye's vault under the Meridian

inventory.name: Dagger of Venom
inventory.note: Acquisitions exhibit A-148, lifted from its glass case in the Undercroft Stores. A slim blade of blued black steel with a green-enamelled hilt, faintly oily to the touch. A plain dagger lies on the black felt in its place, under an unbroken Acquisitions seal.
inventory.source: stolen: Acquisitions case A-148, Cage Three, Undercroft Stores (swapped for a plain dagger)

inventory.description: The Emissary's pin: a closed eye in black enamel on gold, the twin of Crane's coin. Worth perhaps 50 gp to a jeweller; worth a great deal more to whoever it belonged to.
inventory.name: Black-gold closed-eye pin

inventory.description: A folded letter in a foreign hand on heavy cream paper, sealed in black wax with a closed eye. It names its bearer only as 'the Envoy of the Lidless Court' and asks every harbourmaster of the Obsidian Coast to give him passage and no questions.
inventory.name: Letter of passage (Lidless Court)

inventory.description: Heavy gold coins stamped with a rayed sun on one face and a closed eye on the other. A money-changer would give about 25 gp each.
inventory.name: Foreign gold 'sun' coins

inventory.description: A slim silver case for a scent vial, empty. It smells of myrrh.
inventory.name: Silver vial-case

inventory.description: A small black iron key on a silk cord, from round the Emissary's neck. It fits the black lacquer casket.
inventory.name: Casket key on a cord

inventory.name: Page from Faircloth's ledger

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.name: Clothes, Traveler's
inventory.note: Second-hand from Nance Pettle's rag stall: a long brown wool coat gone shiny at the elbows, a grey waistcoat, a flat cloth cap. A clerk's clothes, not a magister's.

inventory.description: Her ladyship's 'terms' for a private masque, signed at the foot in Silas Whitlow's own hand: 'Accepted, on behalf of the Alcazar Players, S. A. Whitlow, Manager', with a looping W and a dash beneath. A clean sample of his signature and hand.

inventory.name: The Magpie's Key
inventory.source: stolen: Lot 9, lifted from Dorothea Quill mid-raid

inventory.description: A heavy coin of dark gold stamped on both sides with a closed eye. The Emissary pays in these. Crane: 'He'll know it if he sees it.'
inventory.name: Black-Gold Coin
inventory.source: gift: Valentin Crane, from his waistcoat

inventory.description: Varga's Meridian Warden sigil: silver, stamped with the sun-and-key. Tuned to the museum's ward lattice. Passes the Bridge of Saints staff gate, the island's outer wards and the galleries after hours, but not the Orrery floor. It becomes an alarm once the Wardens strike Varga's name from their ledger.
inventory.name: Warden's Sigil Ring
inventory.source: stolen: pried off Sergeant Varga's chained hand in the Heron's brig

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: A ready-made gentleman's suit from Faircloth's of Silk Lane: close-cut charcoal worsted coat and waistcoat with dull horn buttons, white shirt, black silk stock, dark trousers, good black boots and a low-crowned black hat. Stylish, quiet, expensive-looking without shining.
inventory.name: Fine clothes (charcoal)
inventory.source: gift: bought by Asche at Faircloth's for 15 gp

inventory.name: Paper
inventory.note: About thirty blank customs clearance forms from before the Council's new quay, kept dry in an oilcloth wrap. Each is headed with the old harbour customs crest and has spaces for vessel, master, cargo, duty paid and the Collector's seal. Good stock for a forger.
inventory.source: found: oilcloth bundle in the clerks' pigeonholes, Old Customs House

inventory.name: Rapier
inventory.note: Valentin Crane's walking cane: black lacquered wood with a silver heron's-head handle. A twist of the handle draws a slim, needle-pointed blade. It passes for a gentleman's cane anywhere a sword would draw looks. The engine treats it as a Rapier.
inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.

inventory.description: A heavy black iron ring set with a gold sun-and-key, warm from the Grand Curator's glove. Her personal sigil: the only key that quiets the plate on her own door below Cage Four.
inventory.name: The Curator's Ring
inventory.source: stolen: tossed to Kit by the charmed Curator, Cage Four

inventory.description: A folded plan of the Rotunda for Gala night in the Curator's hand: concentric rings of seats under the great lens, guests' names in each. The innermost ring holds seven names, the seven Councillors of Vessarine, each marked with a tiny gold sun.
inventory.name: The Gala seating chart

inventory.description: A slim daybook bound in black calf, the Curator's tight hand on every page: appointments, acquisitions, and things she tells no one.
inventory.name: The Curator's daybook

inventory.description: The Curator's own Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame, a gold sun-and-key on the brow, a leather strap. Worn down, it turns the world to dusk.

inventory.description: A Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame with a leather strap.

inventory.description: An iron reliquary the size of a melon, shaped like a closed eye: two curved lids riveted with gold. Inside, the Ysmeran Eye. Cold, heavy, and patient. Do not open the lids without a visor.
inventory.name: The Ysmeran Eye (in its iron reliquary)
inventory.source: stolen: the Eye's vault under the Meridian

inventory.name: Dagger of Venom

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart

inventory.name: Black-Gold Coin
inventory.source: gift: Valentin Crane, from his waistcoat

inventory.description: Varga's Meridian Warden sigil: silver, stamped with the sun-and-key. Tuned to the museum's ward lattice. Passes the Bridge of Saints staff gate, the island's outer wards and the galleries after hours, but not the Orrery floor. It becomes an alarm once the Wardens strike Varga's name from their ledger.
inventory.name: Warden's Sigil Ring
inventory.source: stolen: pried off Sergeant Varga's chained hand in the Heron's brig

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: A ready-made gentleman's suit from Faircloth's of Silk Lane: close-cut charcoal worsted coat and waistcoat with dull horn buttons, white shirt, black silk stock, dark trousers, good black boots and a low-crowned black hat. Stylish, quiet, expensive-looking without shining.
inventory.name: Fine clothes (charcoal)
inventory.source: gift: bought by Asche at Faircloth's for 15 gp

inventory.name: Paper
inventory.note: About thirty blank customs clearance forms from before the Council's new quay, kept dry in an oilcloth wrap. Each is headed with the old harbour customs crest and has spaces for vessel, master, cargo, duty paid and the Collector's seal. Good stock for a forger.
inventory.source: found: oilcloth bundle in the clerks' pigeonholes, Old Customs House

inventory.name: Rapier
inventory.note: Valentin Crane's walking cane: black lacquered wood with a silver heron's-head handle. A twist of the handle draws a slim, needle-pointed blade. It passes for a gentleman's cane anywhere a sword would draw looks. The engine treats it as a Rapier.
inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.
inventory.name: Oilcloth wrap

inventory.description: A heavy black iron ring set with a gold sun-and-key, warm from the Grand Curator's glove. Her personal sigil: the only key that quiets the plate on her own door below Cage Four.
inventory.name: The Curator's Ring
inventory.source: stolen: tossed to Kit by the charmed Curator, Cage Four

inventory.description: A folded plan of the Rotunda for Gala night in the Curator's hand: concentric rings of seats under the great lens, guests' names in each. The innermost ring holds seven names, the seven Councillors of Vessarine, each marked with a tiny gold sun.
inventory.name: The Gala seating chart

inventory.description: A slim daybook bound in black calf, the Curator's tight hand on every page: appointments, acquisitions, and things she tells no one.
inventory.name: The Curator's daybook

inventory.description: The Curator's own Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame, a gold sun-and-key on the brow, a leather strap. Worn down, it turns the world to dusk.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor (gilded, sun-and-key)

inventory.description: A Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame with a leather strap.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor

inventory.description: An iron reliquary the size of a melon, shaped like a closed eye: two curved lids riveted with gold. Inside, the Ysmeran Eye. Cold, heavy, and patient. Do not open the lids without a visor.
inventory.name: The Ysmeran Eye (in its iron reliquary)
inventory.source: stolen: the Eye's vault under the Meridian

inventory.name: Dagger of Venom
inventory.note: Acquisitions exhibit A-148, lifted from its glass case in the Undercroft Stores. A slim blade of blued black steel with a green-enamelled hilt, faintly oily to the touch. A plain dagger lies on the black felt in its place, under an unbroken Acquisitions seal.
inventory.source: stolen: Acquisitions case A-148, Cage Three, Undercroft Stores (swapped for a plain dagger)

inventory.description: The Emissary's pin: a closed eye in black enamel on gold, the twin of Crane's coin. Worth perhaps 50 gp to a jeweller; worth a great deal more to whoever it belonged to.
inventory.name: Black-gold closed-eye pin

inventory.description: A folded letter in a foreign hand on heavy cream paper, sealed in black wax with a closed eye. It names its bearer only as 'the Envoy of the Lidless Court' and asks every harbourmaster of the Obsidian Coast to give him passage and no questions.
inventory.name: Letter of passage (Lidless Court)

inventory.description: Heavy gold coins stamped with a rayed sun on one face and a closed eye on the other. A money-changer would give about 25 gp each.
inventory.name: Foreign gold 'sun' coins

inventory.description: A small black iron key on a silk cord, from round the Emissary's neck. It fits the black lacquer casket.
inventory.name: Casket key on a cord

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

data.text: Kit Corvell is at (24,12) on The Socket.

inventory.description: Lot 9. A masterwork skeleton key of blued steel, its bow shaped like a bird in flight: the Magpie's own. Catalogued as 'removed from exhibit The Thief during routine cleaning.'
inventory.name: The Magpie's Key
inventory.source: stolen: Lot 9, lifted from Dorothea Quill mid-raid

inventory.description: A heavy coin of dark gold stamped on both sides with a closed eye. The Emissary pays in these. Crane: 'He'll know it if he sees it.'
inventory.name: Black-Gold Coin
inventory.source: gift: Valentin Crane, from his waistcoat

inventory.description: Varga's Meridian Warden sigil: silver, stamped with the sun-and-key. Tuned to the museum's ward lattice. Passes the Bridge of Saints staff gate, the island's outer wards and the galleries after hours, but not the Orrery floor. It becomes an alarm once the Wardens strike Varga's name from their ledger.
inventory.name: Warden's Sigil Ring
inventory.source: stolen: pried off Sergeant Varga's chained hand in the Heron's brig

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
inventory.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
inventory.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: A ready-made gentleman's suit from Faircloth's of Silk Lane: close-cut charcoal worsted coat and waistcoat with dull horn buttons, white shirt, black silk stock, dark trousers, good black boots and a low-crowned black hat. Stylish, quiet, expensive-looking without shining.
inventory.name: Fine clothes (charcoal)
inventory.source: gift: bought by Asche at Faircloth's for 15 gp

inventory.name: Paper
inventory.note: About thirty blank customs clearance forms from before the Council's new quay, kept dry in an oilcloth wrap. Each is headed with the old harbour customs crest and has spaces for vessel, master, cargo, duty paid and the Collector's seal. Good stock for a forger.
inventory.source: found: oilcloth bundle in the clerks' pigeonholes, Old Customs House

inventory.name: Rapier
inventory.note: Valentin Crane's walking cane: black lacquered wood with a silver heron's-head handle. A twist of the handle draws a slim, needle-pointed blade. It passes for a gentleman's cane anywhere a sword would draw looks. The engine treats it as a Rapier.
inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.
inventory.name: Oilcloth wrap

inventory.description: A heavy black iron ring set with a gold sun-and-key, warm from the Grand Curator's glove. Her personal sigil: the only key that quiets the plate on her own door below Cage Four.
inventory.name: The Curator's Ring
inventory.source: stolen: tossed to Kit by the charmed Curator, Cage Four

inventory.description: A folded plan of the Rotunda for Gala night in the Curator's hand: concentric rings of seats under the great lens, guests' names in each. The innermost ring holds seven names, the seven Councillors of Vessarine, each marked with a tiny gold sun.
inventory.name: The Gala seating chart

inventory.description: A slim daybook bound in black calf, the Curator's tight hand on every page: appointments, acquisitions, and things she tells no one.
inventory.name: The Curator's daybook

inventory.description: The Curator's own Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame, a gold sun-and-key on the brow, a leather strap. Worn down, it turns the world to dusk.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor (gilded, sun-and-key)

inventory.description: A Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame with a leather strap.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor
Dagger of Venom
inventory.note: Acquisitions exhibit A-148, lifted from its glass case in the Undercroft Stores. A slim blade of blued black steel with a green-enamelled hilt, faintly oily to the touch. A plain dagger lies on the black felt in its place, under an unbroken Acquisitions seal.
inventory.source: stolen: Acquisitions case A-148, Cage Three, Undercroft Stores (swapped for a plain dagger)

inventory.description: The Emissary's pin: a closed eye in black enamel on gold, the twin of Crane's coin. Worth perhaps 50 gp to a jeweller; worth a great deal more to whoever it belonged to.
inventory.name: Black-gold closed-eye pin

inventory.description: A folded letter in a foreign hand on heavy cream paper, sealed in black wax with a closed eye. It names its bearer only as 'the Envoy of the Lidless Court' and asks every harbourmaster of the Obsidian Coast to give him passage and no questions.
inventory.name: Letter of passage (Lidless Court)

inventory.description: Heavy gold coins stamped with a rayed sun on one face and a closed eye on the other. A money-changer would give about 25 gp each.
inventory.name: Foreign gold 'sun' coins

inventory.description: A small black iron key on a silk cord, from round the Emissary's neck. It fits the black lacquer casket.
inventory.name: Casket key on a cord

cmd:
journal add 'Asche'"'"'s ward, fed by the Ysmeran Eye seated in the Socket under the Grey Barrow.

WHERE: the Grey Barrow and the land within a mile of it.

WHAT IT DOES: no one the crew hasn'"'"'t welcomed can find, see or reach the lair. Paths curl back on themselves, the barrow looks like a bare hill, and eyes slide off the doors. A welcomed guest carries a grey token (a chip of barrow stone that Asche has touched to the Eye), or is led in by the hand by someone who carries one. Scrying, locating magic and clairvoyance into it show only grey fog. Someone searching on purpose may feel that something is wrong (Wisdom DC 20), but still can'"'"'t find the way.

WHAT IT DOESN'"'"'T DO: it doesn'"'"'t fight, it doesn'"'"'t hide you once you'"'"'re outside it, and it doesn'"'"'t stop anyone a token-bearer leads in. Only the truly mighty can see through it.

THE HUNGER: at each new moon, a living creature must meet the Eye'"'"'s gaze in the Socket and turn to stone. A missed feeding weakens the Stillness (the DC drops by 5). Miss three and it fails, until it'"'"'s fed three at once.

MOVING THE EYE collapses the Stillness for a day and a night.

It was kindled two years ago with twelve. The next new moon is DAY 7.' --title 'The Stillness'

cmd: journal add 'After the Mole, the crew fled Vessarine over the Saltmarsh Causeway with the Eye and seventy cut gems. They spent most of a year on the road east through four kingdoms, fencing stones a few at a time. On the way Asche found what the Eye truly is (a god'"'"'s soul asleep inside it), and where it could be seated and turned inside out to hide rather than kill: the Grey Barrow, in the Marchwood of the Hollowmark, a forest kingdom in the middle of a civil war. They bought the barrow and its woods from the Abbey of Saint Wendrel and spent two years and a fortune building the Rookery under it. Asche seated the Eye in the old serpent temple'"'"'s Socket and fed it twelve masons, and the Stillness woke. Kept: fifteen gems and about 4,500 crowns. Bought: horses, magic, a household of seven. Nib grew to sixteen under Brakka'"'"'s sword. The chapter opens on Day 1, early spring, in the third year of the Crownless War.' --title 'The Lost Years'

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

pois.name: Ysm-Tharuun
pois.text: A dead city of green stone in the northern Elderwild, choked with roots: towers carved with coiling serpents, a sunken plaza of broken statues, and a stair that goes down into the dark.

pois.name: The Wolf's Tooth
pois.text: A cave mouth in a crag of the Barrow Hills, shaped like a broken fang. Bones at the entrance, and the musk of something big.

pois.name: The Lesser Barrow
pois.text: A second, smaller grey mound deep in the Barrow Hills, with a serpent-carved lintel half buried in bracken. Nobody local will go near it.

pois.name: Witchlight Mere
pois.text: A black mere in the western woods where green lights walk the water at dusk. Drovers go a mile round rather than pass it.

pois.name: The Sunken Road
pois.text: A deep, overgrown holloway east of Ditchley where an old royal road has sunk between its banks. Smugglers' marks cut into the roots.

pois.name: The Gibbet Oak
pois.text: A dead oak at a crossroads south of Brockholt where Harrowgate's justices used to hang thieves. Eleven iron collars still hang in its branches.

pois.name: The Pale Tower
pois.text: A slim white tower with no door at ground level, standing alone on a western hill.

pois.name: Hob's Leap
pois.text: A cleft in a rocky knoll where a stream drops into the dark. Local boys dare each other to the edge.

pois.name: Kingsfell
pois.text: The broken hall of a forgotten royal hunting seat, swallowed by the wood; an antler crown carved over the door.

pois.name: The Hanging Stones
pois.text: A ring of standing stones in the deep wood, each with an iron chain hanging from a hole bored through it.

pois.name: Spiderglen
pois.text: A dark glen strung with webs as thick as rope. Hunters who go in don't come out.

pois.name: The Wardens' Camp
pois.text: A Thornbound warden camp: bark shelters, a sweat-lodge, a lookout platform in an oak.

settlements.name: Elderhaugh
settlements.text: The Thornbound's tree-town: halls and walkways built high in a stand of giant oaks in the heart of the Elderwild, home to a thousand woodfolk and to the Briar Mother's court.

settlements.name: Thornwick
settlements.text: A Thornbound village of turf-roofed longhouses in a clearing ringed with hawthorn.

pois.name: The Heartwood
pois.text: The Thornbound's holiest grove: oaks older than the kingdom, ringed with living thorn and watched over by things that are not entirely trees.

pois.name: The Weeping Yew
pois.text: A vast yew in a hollow of the northern Elderwild that weeps red sap like blood. The Thornbound bury their kings' hearts among its roots.

pois.name: The Green Hollow
pois.text: A drowned-dark valley of the eastern Elderwild where the trees grow black and nothing sings: the lair of a green dragon.

pois.name: Ysm-Tharuun
pois.text: A dead city of green stone in the northern Elderwild, choked with roots: towers carved with coiling serpents, a sunken plaza of broken statues, and a stair that goes down into the dark.

pois.name: The Wolf's Tooth
pois.text: A cave mouth in a crag of the Barrow Hills, shaped like a broken fang. Bones at the entrance, and the musk of something big.

pois.name: The Lesser Barrow
pois.text: A second, smaller grey mound deep in the Barrow Hills, with a serpent-carved lintel half buried in bracken. Nobody local will go near it.

pois.name: Witchlight Mere
pois.text: A black mere in the western woods where green lights walk the water at dusk. Drovers go a mile round rather than pass it.

pois.name: The Sunken Road
pois.text: A deep, overgrown holloway east of Ditchley where an old royal road has sunk between its banks. Smugglers' marks cut into the roots.

pois.name: The Gibbet Oak
pois.text: A dead oak at a crossroads south of Brockholt where Harrowgate's justices used to hang thieves. Eleven iron collars still hang in its branches.

pois.name: The Pale Tower
pois.text: A slim white tower with no door at ground level, standing alone on a western hill.

pois.name: Hob's Leap
pois.text: A cleft in a rocky knoll where a stream drops into the dark. Local boys dare each other to the edge.

pois.name: Kingsfell
pois.text: The broken hall of a forgotten royal hunting seat, swallowed by the wood; an antler crown carved over the door.

pois.name: The Hanging Stones
pois.text: A ring of standing stones in the deep wood, each with an iron chain hanging from a hole bored through it.

pois.name: Spiderglen
pois.text: A dark glen strung with webs as thick as rope. Hunters who go in don't come out.

pois.name: The Wardens' Camp
pois.text: A Thornbound warden camp: bark shelters, a sweat-lodge, a lookout platform in an oak.

pois.name: The Old Watch
pois.text: A ruined watchtower on a spur of the Greyspine, older than the Hollowmark.

settlements.name: Elderhaugh
settlements.text: The Thornbound's tree-town: halls and walkways built high in a stand of giant oaks in the heart of the Elderwild, home to a thousand woodfolk and to the Briar Mother's court.

settlements.name: Thornwick
settlements.text: A Thornbound village of turf-roofed longhouses in a clearing ringed with hawthorn.

settlements.name: Yew Hollow
settlements.text: A hidden Thornbound steading among ancient yews; the folk there paint their faces green for the old rites.

pois.text: A dead city of green stone in the northern Elderwild, choked with roots: towers carved with coiling serpents, a sunken plaza of broken statues, and a stair that goes down into the dark.

pois.name: The Wolf's Tooth
pois.text: A cave mouth in a crag of the Barrow Hills, shaped like a broken fang. Bones at the entrance, and the musk of something big.

pois.name: The Lesser Barrow
pois.text: A second, smaller grey mound deep in the Barrow Hills, with a serpent-carved lintel half buried in bracken. Nobody local will go near it.

pois.name: Witchlight Mere
pois.text: A black mere in the western woods where green lights walk the water at dusk. Drovers go a mile round rather than pass it.

pois.name: The Sunken Road
pois.text: A deep, overgrown holloway east of Ditchley where an old royal road has sunk between its banks. Smugglers' marks cut into the roots.

pois.name: The Gibbet Oak
pois.text: A dead oak at a crossroads south of Brockholt where Harrowgate's justices used to hang thieves. Eleven iron collars still hang in its branches.

pois.name: The Pale Tower
pois.text: A slim white tower with no door at ground level, standing alone on a western hill.

pois.name: Hob's Leap
pois.text: A cleft in a rocky knoll where a stream drops into the dark. Local boys dare each other to the edge.

pois.name: Kingsfell
pois.text: The broken hall of a forgotten royal hunting seat, swallowed by the wood; an antler crown carved over the door.

pois.name: The Hanging Stones
pois.text: A ring of standing stones in the deep wood, each with an iron chain hanging from a hole bored through it.

pois.name: Spiderglen
pois.text: A dark glen strung with webs as thick as rope. Hunters who go in don't come out.

inventory.description: Lot 9. A masterwork skeleton key of blued steel, its bow shaped like a bird in flight: the Magpie's own. Catalogued as 'removed from exhibit The Thief during routine cleaning.'
inventory.name: The Magpie's Key
inventory.source: stolen: Lot 9, lifted from Dorothea Quill mid-raid

inventory.description: A ready-made gentleman's suit from Faircloth's of Silk Lane: close-cut charcoal worsted coat and waistcoat with dull horn buttons, white shirt, black silk stock, dark trousers, good black boots and a low-crowned black hat. Stylish, quiet, expensive-looking without shining.
inventory.name: Fine clothes (charcoal)
inventory.source: gift: bought by Asche at Faircloth's for 15 gp

inventory.name: Paper
inventory.note: About thirty blank customs clearance forms from before the Council's new quay, kept dry in an oilcloth wrap. Each is headed with the old harbour customs crest and has spaces for vessel, master, cargo, duty paid and the Collector's seal. Good stock for a forger.
inventory.source: found: oilcloth bundle in the clerks' pigeonholes, Old Customs House

inventory.name: Rapier
inventory.note: Valentin Crane's walking cane: black lacquered wood with a silver heron's-head handle. A twist of the handle draws a slim, needle-pointed blade. It passes for a gentleman's cane anywhere a sword would draw looks. The engine treats it as a Rapier.
inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.
inventory.name: Oilcloth wrap

inventory.description: A Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame with a leather strap.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor
Dagger of Venom
inventory.note: Acquisitions exhibit A-148, lifted from its glass case in the Undercroft Stores. A slim blade of blued black steel with a green-enamelled hilt, faintly oily to the touch. A plain dagger lies on the black felt in its place, under an unbroken Acquisitions seal.
inventory.source: stolen: Acquisitions case A-148, Cage Three, Undercroft Stores (swapped for a plain dagger)

inventory.description: The Emissary's pin: a closed eye in black enamel on gold, the twin of Crane's coin. Worth perhaps 50 gp to a jeweller; worth a great deal more to whoever it belonged to.
inventory.name: Black-gold closed-eye pin

inventory.description: A folded letter in a foreign hand on heavy cream paper, sealed in black wax with a closed eye. It names its bearer only as 'the Envoy of the Lidless Court' and asks every harbourmaster of the Obsidian Coast to give him passage and no questions.
inventory.name: Letter of passage (Lidless Court)

inventory.description: Heavy gold coins stamped with a rayed sun on one face and a closed eye on the other. A money-changer would give about 25 gp each.
inventory.name: Foreign gold 'sun' coins

inventory.description: A small black iron key on a silk cord, from round the Emissary's neck. It fits the black lacquer casket.
inventory.name: Casket key on a cord
Mule
inventory.note: The grey mule taken with the cart on the March Road. Its near-hind shoe is cracked, leaving a forked print: it wants a farrier.
inventory.source: stolen: the Rookery's own mule, back from the Hanged Men's horse line

inventory.name: Book
inventory.note: A thumb-sized book bound in greasy calfskin, its pages ruled in columns in a small neat hand, with a stub of pencil tied to the spine. It was under the pillow in the big tent, wrapped in a stocking.
inventory.source: found: under the woman's pillow in the big tent

inventory.description: A letter in a soldier's square hand, from Lucan Mire to Sir Gerold Ambry of Harrowgate, offering his twelve men for the Fallowfield lands and a title. It breaks off mid-sentence.
inventory.name: Lucan's unfinished letter

inventory.description: The Emissary's casket: black lacquer, a closed eye in gold on the lid, black silk inside. Sixty cut gemstones in four rows (sapphires, rubies, emeralds and pale diamonds), each worth about 1,000 gp to an honest jeweller. 60,000 gp in all. Unlocked; the key is on a cord in Kit's coat.
inventory.name: Black lacquer casket of cut gems
inventory.note: The Emissary's black lacquer casket, a closed eye in gold on the lid. Fifteen cut gemstones remain on the black silk, about 1,000 gp each (15,000 gp): the crew's reserve. Forty-five of the sixty were fenced in the lost years to build the lair. Kit has the key on its cord.
inventory.source: loot: the Emissary's casket, the north room

item.description: A heavy black iron ring set with a gold sun-and-key, warm from the Grand Curator's glove. Her personal sigil: the only key that quiets the plate on her own door below Cage Four.
item.name: The Curator's Ring
item.source: stolen: tossed to Kit by the charmed Curator, Cage Four

item.description: A folded plan of the Rotunda for Gala night in the Curator's hand: concentric rings of seats under the great lens, guests' names in each. The innermost ring holds seven names, the seven Councillors of Vessarine, each marked with a tiny gold sun.
item.name: The Gala seating chart

item.description: A slim daybook bound in black calf, the Curator's tight hand on every page: appointments, acquisitions, and things she tells no one.
item.name: The Curator's daybook

item.description: The Curator's own Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame, a gold sun-and-key on the brow, a leather strap. Worn down, it turns the world to dusk.
item.name: Smoked-glass visor (gilded, sun-and-key)

item.description: Varga's Meridian Warden sigil: silver, stamped with the sun-and-key. Tuned to the museum's ward lattice. Passes the Bridge of Saints staff gate, the island's outer wards and the galleries after hours, but not the Orrery floor. It becomes an alarm once the Wardens strike Varga's name from their ledger.
item.name: Warden's Sigil Ring
item.source: stolen: pried off Sergeant Varga's chained hand in the Heron's brig

item.description: A heavy coin of dark gold stamped on both sides with a closed eye. The Emissary pays in these. Crane: 'He'll know it if he sees it.'
item.name: Black-Gold Coin
item.source: gift: Valentin Crane, from his waistcoat

item.description: Captain Thorne's own visor: smoked glass in a heavy brass frame with a snapped leather strap, torn off his helm on the Curator's stair.
item.name: Thorne's smoked-glass visor
item.source: loot: torn off Captain Thorne's helm

item.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'
item.name: Emeric Dane's Last Letter
item.source: gift: lent by Wynn Dane to 'the chapel' for the Saint's Book of Remembrance; she wants it back

inventory.description: A ready-made gentleman's suit from Faircloth's of Silk Lane: close-cut charcoal worsted coat and waistcoat with dull horn buttons, white shirt, black silk stock, dark trousers, good black boots and a low-crowned black hat. Stylish, quiet, expensive-looking without shining.
inventory.name: Fine clothes (charcoal)
inventory.source: gift: bought by Asche at Faircloth's for 15 gp

inventory.name: Paper
inventory.note: About thirty blank customs clearance forms from before the Council's new quay, kept dry in an oilcloth wrap. Each is headed with the old harbour customs crest and has spaces for vessel, master, cargo, duty paid and the Collector's seal. Good stock for a forger.
inventory.source: found: oilcloth bundle in the clerks' pigeonholes, Old Customs House

inventory.name: Rapier
inventory.note: Valentin Crane's walking cane: black lacquered wood with a silver heron's-head handle. A twist of the handle draws a slim, needle-pointed blade. It passes for a gentleman's cane anywhere a sword would draw looks. The engine treats it as a Rapier.
inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.
inventory.name: Oilcloth wrap

inventory.description: A Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame with a leather strap.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor
Dagger of Venom
inventory.note: Acquisitions exhibit A-148, lifted from its glass case in the Undercroft Stores. A slim blade of blued black steel with a green-enamelled hilt, faintly oily to the touch. A plain dagger lies on the black felt in its place, under an unbroken Acquisitions seal.
inventory.source: stolen: Acquisitions case A-148, Cage Three, Undercroft Stores (swapped for a plain dagger)

inventory.description: The Emissary's pin: a closed eye in black enamel on gold, the twin of Crane's coin. Worth perhaps 50 gp to a jeweller; worth a great deal more to whoever it belonged to.
inventory.name: Black-gold closed-eye pin

inventory.description: A folded letter in a foreign hand on heavy cream paper, sealed in black wax with a closed eye. It names its bearer only as 'the Envoy of the Lidless Court' and asks every harbourmaster of the Obsidian Coast to give him passage and no questions.
inventory.name: Letter of passage (Lidless Court)

inventory.description: Heavy gold coins stamped with a rayed sun on one face and a closed eye on the other. A money-changer would give about 25 gp each.
inventory.name: Foreign gold 'sun' coins

inventory.description: A small black iron key on a silk cord, from round the Emissary's neck. It fits the black lacquer casket.
inventory.name: Casket key on a cord
Mule
inventory.note: The grey mule taken with the cart on the March Road. Its near-hind shoe is cracked, leaving a forked print: it wants a farrier.
inventory.source: stolen: the Rookery's own mule, back from the Hanged Men's horse line

inventory.name: Book
inventory.note: A thumb-sized book bound in greasy calfskin, its pages ruled in columns in a small neat hand, with a stub of pencil tied to the spine. It was under the pillow in the big tent, wrapped in a stocking.
inventory.source: found: under the woman's pillow in the big tent

inventory.description: A letter in a soldier's square hand, from Lucan Mire to Sir Gerold Ambry of Harrowgate, offering his twelve men for the Fallowfield lands and a title. It breaks off mid-sentence.
inventory.name: Lucan's unfinished letter

inventory.description: The Emissary's casket: black lacquer, a closed eye in gold on the lid, black silk inside. inventory.name: Black lacquer casket of cut gems
inventory.note: The Emissary's black lacquer casket, a closed eye in gold on the lid. Fifteen cut gemstones remain on the black silk, about 1,000 gp each (15,000 gp): the crew's reserve. Forty-five of the sixty were fenced in the lost years to build the lair. Kit has the key on its cord.
inventory.source: loot: the Emissary's casket, the north room

inventory.name: Rapier
inventory.note: Valentin Crane's walking cane: black lacquered wood with a silver heron's-head handle. A twist of the handle draws a slim, needle-pointed blade. It passes for a gentleman's cane anywhere a sword would draw looks. The engine treats it as a Rapier.
inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.

inventory.description: A Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame with a leather strap.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor
Dagger of Venom
inventory.note: Acquisitions exhibit A-148, lifted from its glass case in the Undercroft Stores. A slim blade of blued black steel with a green-enamelled hilt, faintly oily to the touch. A plain dagger lies on the black felt in its place, under an unbroken Acquisitions seal.
inventory.source: stolen: Acquisitions case A-148, Cage Three, Undercroft Stores (swapped for a plain dagger)

inventory.description: The Emissary's pin: a closed eye in black enamel on gold, the twin of Crane's coin. Worth perhaps 50 gp to a jeweller; worth a great deal more to whoever it belonged to.
inventory.name: Black-gold closed-eye pin

inventory.description: A folded letter in a foreign hand on heavy cream paper, sealed in black wax with a closed eye. It names its bearer only as 'the Envoy of the Lidless Court' and asks every harbourmaster of the Obsidian Coast to give him passage and no questions.
inventory.name: Letter of passage (Lidless Court)

inventory.description: Heavy gold coins stamped with a rayed sun on one face and a closed eye on the other. A money-changer would give about 25 gp each.
inventory.name: Foreign gold 'sun' coins

inventory.description: A small black iron key on a silk cord, from round the Emissary's neck. It fits the black lacquer casket.
inventory.name: Casket key on a cord
Mule
inventory.note: The grey mule taken with the cart on the March Road. Its near-hind shoe is cracked, leaving a forked print: it wants a farrier.
inventory.source: stolen: the Rookery's own mule, back from the Hanged Men's horse line

inventory.name: Book
inventory.note: A thumb-sized book bound in greasy calfskin, its pages ruled in columns in a small neat hand, with a stub of pencil tied to the spine. It was under the pillow in the big tent, wrapped in a stocking.

inventory.description: A letter in a soldier's square hand, from Lucan Mire to Sir Gerold Ambry of Harrowgate, offering his twelve men for the Fallowfield lands and a title. It breaks off mid-sentence.

inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor

inventory.description: Heavy gold coins stamped with a rayed sun on one face and a closed eye on the other. A money-changer would give about 25 gp each.

inventory.name: Fine clothes (charcoal)
inventory.source: gift: bought by Asche at Faircloth's for 15 gp

inventory.name: Paper

inventory.name: Rapier

inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.
inventory.name: Oilcloth wrap

inventory.description: A Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame with a leather strap.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor
Dagger of Venom

inventory.source: stolen: Acquisitions case A-148, Cage Three, Undercroft Stores (swapped for a plain dagger)

inventory.description: The Emissary's pin: a closed eye in black enamel on gold, the twin of Crane's coin. Worth perhaps 50 gp to a jeweller; worth a great deal more to whoever it belonged to.
inventory.name: Black-gold closed-eye pin

inventory.description: A folded letter in a foreign hand on heavy cream paper, sealed in black wax with a closed eye. It names its bearer only as 'the Envoy of the Lidless Court' and asks every harbourmaster of the Obsidian Coast to give him passage and no questions.
inventory.name: Letter of passage (Lidless Court)

inventory.description: Heavy gold coins stamped with a rayed sun on one face and a closed eye on the other. A money-changer would give about 25 gp each.
inventory.name: Foreign gold 'sun' coins

inventory.description: A small black iron key on a silk cord, from round the Emissary's neck. It fits the black lacquer casket.
inventory.name: Casket key on a cord

inventory.description: Lot 9. A masterwork skeleton key of blued steel, its bow shaped like a bird in flight: the Magpie's own. Catalogued as 'removed from exhibit The Thief during routine cleaning.'
inventory.name: The Magpie's Key
inventory.source: stolen: Lot 9, lifted from Dorothea Quill mid-raid

inventory.description: A ready-made gentleman's suit from Faircloth's of Silk Lane: close-cut charcoal worsted coat and waistcoat with dull horn buttons, white shirt, black silk stock, dark trousers, good black boots and a low-crowned black hat. Stylish, quiet, expensive-looking without shining.
inventory.name: Fine clothes (charcoal)
inventory.source: gift: bought by Asche at Faircloth's for 15 gp

inventory.name: Paper
inventory.note: About thirty blank customs clearance forms from before the Council's new quay, kept dry in an oilcloth wrap. Each is headed with the old harbour customs crest and has spaces for vessel, master, cargo, duty paid and the Collector's seal. Good stock for a forger.
inventory.source: found: oilcloth bundle in the clerks' pigeonholes, Old Customs House

inventory.name: Rapier
inventory.note: Valentin Crane's walking cane: black lacquered wood with a silver heron's-head handle. A twist of the handle draws a slim, needle-pointed blade. It passes for a gentleman's cane anywhere a sword would draw looks. The engine treats it as a Rapier.
inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.
inventory.name: Oilcloth wrap

inventory.description: A Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame with a leather strap.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor
Dagger of Venom
inventory.note: Acquisitions exhibit A-148, lifted from its glass case in the Undercroft Stores. A slim blade of blued black steel with a green-enamelled hilt, faintly oily to the touch. A plain dagger lies on the black felt in its place, under an unbroken Acquisitions seal.
inventory.source: stolen: Acquisitions case A-148, Cage Three, Undercroft Stores (swapped for a plain dagger)

inventory.description: The Emissary's pin: a closed eye in black enamel on gold, the twin of Crane's coin. Worth perhaps 50 gp to a jeweller; worth a great deal more to whoever it belonged to.
inventory.name: Black-gold closed-eye pin

inventory.description: A folded letter in a foreign hand on heavy cream paper, sealed in black wax with a closed eye. It names its bearer only as 'the Envoy of the Lidless Court' and asks every harbourmaster of the Obsidian Coast to give him passage and no questions.
inventory.name: Letter of passage (Lidless Court)

inventory.description: Heavy gold coins stamped with a rayed sun on one face and a closed eye on the other. A money-changer would give about 25 gp each.
inventory.name: Foreign gold 'sun' coins

inventory.description: A small black iron key on a silk cord, from round the Emissary's neck. It fits the black lacquer casket.
inventory.name: Casket key on a cord
Mule
inventory.note: The grey mule taken with the cart on the March Road. Its near-hind shoe is cracked, leaving a forked print: it wants a farrier.
inventory.source: stolen: the Rookery's own mule, back from the Hanged Men's horse line

inventory.name: Book
inventory.note: A thumb-sized book bound in greasy calfskin, its pages ruled in columns in a small neat hand, with a stub of pencil tied to the spine. It was under the pillow in the big tent, wrapped in a stocking.
inventory.source: found: under the woman's pillow in the big tent

inventory.description: A letter in a soldier's square hand, from Lucan Mire to Sir Gerold Ambry of Harrowgate, offering his twelve men for the Fallowfield lands and a title. It breaks off mid-sentence.
inventory.name: Lucan's unfinished letter

inventory.description: A letter of credit on the Charter League's Thornbury house for 7,000 crowns, payable to the bearer on sight, signed by Master Pell and sealed with the League's scales. Cash it at the League factor's house in Thornbury.
inventory.name: League letter of credit
inventory.note: Payable to the bearer on sight at the League factor's house in Thornbury, signed by Master Pell, sealed with the League's scales.

inventory.description: A small black iron key on a silk cord, from round the Emissary's neck. It fits the black lacquer casket.
inventory.name: Casket key on a cord

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'

inventory.description: A letter of credit on the Charter League's Thornbury house for 7,000 crowns, payable to the bearer on sight, signed by Master Pell and sealed with the League's scales. Cash it at the League factor's house in Thornbury.
inventory.name: League letter of credit
inventory.note: Payable to the bearer on sight at the League factor's house in Thornbury, signed by Master Pell, sealed with the League's scales.
inventory.source: reward: sale of fifteen gems to the Charter League

data.text: Kit Corvell gives 1× League letter of credit to Master Pell.

coins kit +1800gp --source 'reward: Master Pell discounts the League letter of credit (1,800 of 6,300 in coin)'
