inventory.description: Lot 9. A masterwork skeleton key of blued steel, its bow shaped like a bird in flight: the Magpie's own. Catalogued as 'removed from exhibit The Thief during routine cleaning.'
inventory.name: The Magpie's Key
inventory.source: stolen: Lot 9, lifted from Dorothea Quill mid-raid

inventory.description: A ready-made gentleman's suit from Faircloth's of Silk Lane: close-cut charcoal worsted coat and waistcoat with dull horn buttons, white shirt, black silk stock, dark trousers, good black boots and a low-crowned black hat. Stylish, quiet, expensive-looking without shining.
inventory.name: Fine clothes (charcoal)
inventory.source: gift: bought by Asche at Faircloth's for 15 gp

inventory.name: Paper
inventory.note: About thirty blank customs clearance forms from before the Council's new quay, kept dry in an oilcloth wrap. Each is headed with the old harbour customs crest and has spaces for vessel, master, cargo, duty paid and the Collector's seal. Good stock for a forger.
inventory.source: found: oilcloth bundle in the clerks' pigeonholes, Old Customs House

inventory.name: Rapier
inventory.note: Valentin Crane's walking cane: black lacquered wood with a silver heron's-head handle. A twist of the handle draws a slim, needle-pointed blade. It passes for a gentleman's cane anywhere a sword would draw looks. The engine treats it as a Rapier.
inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.
inventory.name: Oilcloth wrap

inventory.description: A Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame with a leather strap.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor
Dagger of Venom
inventory.note: Acquisitions exhibit A-148, lifted from its glass case in the Undercroft Stores. A slim blade of blued black steel with a green-enamelled hilt, faintly oily to the touch. A plain dagger lies on the black felt in its place, under an unbroken Acquisitions seal.
inventory.source: stolen: Acquisitions case A-148, Cage Three, Undercroft Stores (swapped for a plain dagger)

inventory.description: The Emissary's pin: a closed eye in black enamel on gold, the twin of Crane's coin. Worth perhaps 50 gp to a jeweller; worth a great deal more to whoever it belonged to.
inventory.name: Black-gold closed-eye pin

inventory.description: A folded letter in a foreign hand on heavy cream paper, sealed in black wax with a closed eye. It names its bearer only as 'the Envoy of the Lidless Court' and asks every harbourmaster of the Obsidian Coast to give him passage and no questions.
inventory.name: Letter of passage (Lidless Court)

inventory.description: Heavy gold coins stamped with a rayed sun on one face and a closed eye on the other. A money-changer would give about 25 gp each.
inventory.name: Foreign gold 'sun' coins

inventory.description: A small black iron key on a silk cord, from round the Emissary's neck. It fits the black lacquer casket.
inventory.name: Casket key on a cord
Mule
inventory.note: The grey mule taken with the cart on the March Road. Its near-hind shoe is cracked, leaving a forked print: it wants a farrier.
inventory.source: stolen: the Rookery's own mule, back from the Hanged Men's horse line

inventory.name: Book
inventory.note: A thumb-sized book bound in greasy calfskin, its pages ruled in columns in a small neat hand, with a stub of pencil tied to the spine. It was under the pillow in the big tent, wrapped in a stocking.
inventory.source: found: under the woman's pillow in the big tent

inventory.description: A letter in a soldier's square hand, from Lucan Mire to Sir Gerold Ambry of Harrowgate, offering his twelve men for the Fallowfield lands and a title. It breaks off mid-sentence.
inventory.name: Lucan's unfinished letter

inventory.description: trinket
inventory.name: Silver eye pendant

inventory.description: an iron eye on a chain, the holy symbol of the Lidless church
inventory.name: Iron eye holy symbol

inventory.description: a dozen letters tied with grey ribbon, several under a seal of an open eye, from Ennis's strongbox (unread)
inventory.name: Bundle of sealed letters

inventory.description: a folded writ under Harrowgate's seal (a tower and a stag), from Sergeant Thorley's belt pouch, singed at one corner (unread)
inventory.name: Sealed orders of Sir Gerold

inventory.description: A long roll of heavy paper in an oiled-leather tube under the Regency's antler seal: the Marchwood's war-tax for the season, village by village, landholder by landholder, what was assessed, what was paid and what is still owed, in a clerk's tight hand. Unread.
inventory.name: The Marchwood tally-roll
inventory.source: loot: the oiled-leather tube strapped inside the tax wagon's tailboard

inventory.description: In Quist's careful hand (a little shakier on the left margins): a bill of sale for the assignment of Sir Gerold Ambry's debt of six thousand crowns from the Charter League to 'the Lord of Crowsfoot', with the price left blank; and a printed form of loan at one in ten a month, secured upon the borrower's land, with spaces for name, sum and seal.
inventory.name: Quist's papers
inventory.source: gift: drawn by Quist that evening

inventory.description: A heavy, long-shanked iron key on a fine steel chain, warm from a dead man's throat, its bow cast in the shape of the League's scales.
inventory.name: The factor's key

inventory.description: A heavy iron ring of a dozen house keys of every size, from the coat pegs on the League house landing.
inventory.name: The League house key ring
inventory.source: loot: the coat pegs on the League house landing

inventory.description: A gold brooch set with a dark red garnet in a ring of seed pearls, a woman's Sunday best; worth perhaps fifteen crowns.
inventory.name: Garnet brooch

inventory.description: A pair of carved jet drop earrings on gold wires, mourning jewellery; worth perhaps ten crowns.
inventory.name: Jet earrings

inventory.description: The Thornbury house's brass desk seal: the Charter League's scales above the word THORNBURY, on a turned walnut handle, with a stick of the League's green sealing wax. Any paper sealed with it looks like the League's own.
inventory.name: The League's seal
inventory.source: stolen: the factor's desk in the League counting room

inventory.description: A sheaf of a dozen printed League letter-of-credit blanks on heavy watermarked paper, the scales printed at the head, spaces for sum, bearer, house and the factor's hand. Unsigned and unsealed.
inventory.name: Blank League letters of credit
inventory.source: stolen: a locked drawer in the League counting room

inventory.description: A heavy parchment bond under Sir Gerold Ambry's seal and the League's scales: six thousand crowns lent to the castellan of Harrowgate against the revenues of Ditchley and his own estate, interest at one in twenty a quarter, two quarters already in arrears. Whoever holds it can call the debt, or sell it.
inventory.name: Sir Gerold's bond

inventory.description: A fat green-bound register: every League letter of credit drawn on the Thornbury house for five years, by number, sum, date and bearer, with the factor's notes. Your own seven thousand is entered on the last written page.
inventory.name: The League's register of letters

inventory.description: Two chests' worth of papers held as surety, tied in labelled bundles: loans to the miller at Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant's landlord and a dozen Marchwood freeholders, each with the borrower's seal and the sum owed. Together they record a little over four thousand crowns owed to the League by men who live within thirty miles.
inventory.name: Bundle of League bonds and deeds

inventory.description: Six packets of the factor's correspondence tied in green tape and sealed, some from the League's masters at Gildford, unread.
inventory.name: Sealed League packets

inventory.description: Four green bond-books: the Thornbury house's accounts with every borrower for fifteen years, in the factor's tidy hand.
inventory.name: The League's bond-books

inventory.description: A deed of assignment on the League's own watermarked paper, in Factor Ambrose Leck's precise hand to the life, dated eight days ago and sealed in Thornbury green with the house's brass seal: the Charter League, for value received, assigns to the Lord of Crowsfoot all its right in the bonds of Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant and twelve Marchwood freeholders (schedule attached). A forgery good enough to fool the man who wrote the hand (Ottilie's work: 24).
inventory.name: The League's assignment of bonds
inventory.source: crafted: Ottilie's forgery at the Crow and Kettle

inventory.description: A Charter League letter of credit for two thousand crowns, payable to bearer at the League's Gildford house, in Master Pell's hand under the scales seal.
inventory.name: Pell's letter on Gildford (2,000)
inventory.source: reward: Master Pell, for the Thornbury letter

cmd: show text 'QUIST'"'"'S MORNING REPORT, DAY 14. IN HAND: the great strongbox, 15,111 crowns. On his lordship: 100 crowns; Master Pell'"'"'s letters, 1,000 on Gildford and 1,500 on Kingsholt; a garnet brooch and jet earrings (about 25). PAPER: Sir Gerold'"'"'s bond, 6,000 at one in twenty a quarter, two quarters (600) in arrears. The League'"'"'s assignment to us of about 4,000 crowns of Marchwood bonds (Oxbow Mill, the moated farm, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant, twelve freeholders). The League'"'"'s Thornbury seal and a dozen blank letters. The League'"'"'s register and bond-books. The Marchwood tally-roll. PROPERTY: the Rookery. Coldharbour (deed in hand; works under way). Crowsfoot under the Hanged Men, the fort half built. COMING IN: the Hanged Men'"'"'s third, Day 16 (about 60). Lerner and Harl with the arrears and recruits, Day 17 (unknown). Coldharbour'"'"'s first takings, Day 30 (about 100). Pell cashes Moss'"'"'s letter, Day 20 (Moss'"'"'s, not ours). GOING OUT: wages 430, Day 30. Two supply carts, about 300 a month. The fort'"'"'s second month, about 4,000, Day 34, and a third after. Captain Lerner'"'"'s reward, when earned. THE SUM: about 750 a month out and about 350 in, before the fort. With the fort we stand near 6,000 by midsummer; without it, over 14,000. OPEN ITEMS: 1. Collect on the assigned bonds before the League'"'"'s word spreads. 2. Gerold'"'"'s bond: call it, sell it, or hold it over him. 3. Present Pell'"'"'s two letters at Gildford and Kingsholt. 4. Sell the brooch and earrings. 5. The tally-roll, unread. 6. The prisoners (Bastian). 7. The new moon, Day 37. 8. Harrowgate'"'"'s letters to Castle Gaunt and the Regent: an answer may come any day. 9. The Thornbury house will have been found yesterday morning. 10. The Mother Sabine, '"'"'before the month turns'"'"'.' --title 'Quist'"'"'s morning report, Day 14'

cmd: show text 'THE SIX LEAGUE PACKETS (Thornbury house, from the masters at Gildford; read by Quist). 1. RATES: the spring rates for credit and exchange; Thornbury to keep no more than 3,000 in coin '"'"'while the March is unquiet'"'"'. 2. THE CROWN (Day 2): '"'"'No further credit to Kingsholt or Castle Gaunt on any terms. The Crown'"'"'s debt to the League stands at ninety thousand crowns; the Lord Protector asks for twenty more against the Holdfast silver. Refuse. If the Midsummer crowning goes forward we shall have to decide whom we are lending to.'"'"' 3. HARROWGATE: '"'"'Sir Gerold Ambry is two quarters in arrears. Press him civilly; if he has not paid by Midsummer, the bond is to be called and his tenancy of Ditchley sold.'"'"' 4. A QUERY: '"'"'Report what you learn of the foreign lord at Crowsfoot who sells old Vessarine stones, his household and his purse. The masters take an interest.'"'"' 5. CARRIERS: the summer schedule of the League'"'"'s carts on the Pilgrim Road and the Amber Road (dates, guards, the Gildford-Kingsholt silver cart on the fourth of each month). 6. A PRIVATE NOTE to Leck from a colleague at Ambersell: '"'"'The Watchful Mission here has bought a great deal of credit lately against a caravan it means to send west in early summer under heavy guard. Whatever they are carrying, they will not say.'"'"'' --title 'The six League packets'

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.

inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor

inventory.description: A sheaf of a dozen printed League letter-of-credit blanks on heavy watermarked paper, the scales printed at the head, spaces for sum, bearer, house and the factor's hand. Unsigned and unsealed.

inventory.description: Six packets of the factor's correspondence tied in green tape and sealed, some from the League's masters at Gildford, unread.
inventory.name: Sealed League packets

inventory.description: Four green bond-books: the Thornbury house's accounts with every borrower for fifteen years, in the factor's tidy hand.
inventory.name: The League's bond-books

inventory.description: A deed of assignment on the League's own watermarked paper, in Factor Ambrose Leck's precise hand to the life, dated eight days ago and sealed in Thornbury green with the house's brass seal: the Charter League, for value received, assigns to the Lord of Crowsfoot all its right in the bonds of Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant and twelve Marchwood freeholders (schedule attached). inventory.description: Lot 9. A masterwork skeleton key of blued steel, its bow shaped like a bird in flight: the Magpie's own. Catalogued as 'removed from exhibit The Thief during routine cleaning.'
inventory.name: The Magpie's Key
inventory.source: stolen: Lot 9, lifted from Dorothea Quill mid-raid

inventory.description: A ready-made gentleman's suit from Faircloth's of Silk Lane: close-cut charcoal worsted coat and waistcoat with dull horn buttons, white shirt, black silk stock, dark trousers, good black boots and a low-crowned black hat. Stylish, quiet, expensive-looking without shining.
inventory.name: Fine clothes (charcoal)
inventory.source: gift: bought by Asche at Faircloth's for 15 gp

inventory.name: Paper
inventory.note: About thirty blank customs clearance forms from before the Council's new quay, kept dry in an oilcloth wrap. Each is headed with the old harbour customs crest and has spaces for vessel, master, cargo, duty paid and the Collector's seal. Good stock for a forger.
inventory.source: found: oilcloth bundle in the clerks' pigeonholes, Old Customs House

inventory.name: Rapier
inventory.note: Valentin Crane's walking cane: black lacquered wood with a silver heron's-head handle. A twist of the handle draws a slim, needle-pointed blade. It passes for a gentleman's cane anywhere a sword would draw looks. The engine treats it as a Rapier.
inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.
inventory.name: Oilcloth wrap

inventory.description: A Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame with a leather strap.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor
Dagger of Venom
inventory.note: Acquisitions exhibit A-148, lifted from its glass case in the Undercroft Stores. A slim blade of blued black steel with a green-enamelled hilt, faintly oily to the touch. A plain dagger lies on the black felt in its place, under an unbroken Acquisitions seal.
inventory.source: stolen: Acquisitions case A-148, Cage Three, Undercroft Stores (swapped for a plain dagger)

inventory.description: The Emissary's pin: a closed eye in black enamel on gold, the twin of Crane's coin. Worth perhaps 50 gp to a jeweller; worth a great deal more to whoever it belonged to.
inventory.name: Black-gold closed-eye pin

inventory.description: A folded letter in a foreign hand on heavy cream paper, sealed in black wax with a closed eye. It names its bearer only as 'the Envoy of the Lidless Court' and asks every harbourmaster of the Obsidian Coast to give him passage and no questions.
inventory.name: Letter of passage (Lidless Court)

inventory.description: Heavy gold coins stamped with a rayed sun on one face and a closed eye on the other. A money-changer would give about 25 gp each.
inventory.name: Foreign gold 'sun' coins

inventory.description: A small black iron key on a silk cord, from round the Emissary's neck. It fits the black lacquer casket.
inventory.name: Casket key on a cord
Mule
inventory.note: The grey mule taken with the cart on the March Road. Its near-hind shoe is cracked, leaving a forked print: it wants a farrier.
inventory.source: stolen: the Rookery's own mule, back from the Hanged Men's horse line

inventory.name: Book
inventory.note: A thumb-sized book bound in greasy calfskin, its pages ruled in columns in a small neat hand, with a stub of pencil tied to the spine. It was under the pillow in the big tent, wrapped in a stocking.
inventory.source: found: under the woman's pillow in the big tent

inventory.description: A letter in a soldier's square hand, from Lucan Mire to Sir Gerold Ambry of Harrowgate, offering his twelve men for the Fallowfield lands and a title. It breaks off mid-sentence.
inventory.name: Lucan's unfinished letter

inventory.description: trinket
inventory.name: Silver eye pendant

inventory.description: an iron eye on a chain, the holy symbol of the Lidless church
inventory.name: Iron eye holy symbol

inventory.description: a dozen letters tied with grey ribbon, several under a seal of an open eye, from Ennis's strongbox (unread)
inventory.name: Bundle of sealed letters

inventory.description: a folded writ under Harrowgate's seal (a tower and a stag), from Sergeant Thorley's belt pouch, singed at one corner (unread)
inventory.name: Sealed orders of Sir Gerold

inventory.description: A long roll of heavy paper in an oiled-leather tube under the Regency's antler seal: the Marchwood's war-tax for the season, village by village, landholder by landholder, what was assessed, what was paid and what is still owed, in a clerk's tight hand. Unread.
inventory.name: The Marchwood tally-roll
inventory.source: loot: the oiled-leather tube strapped inside the tax wagon's tailboard

inventory.description: In Quist's careful hand (a little shakier on the left margins): a bill of sale for the assignment of Sir Gerold Ambry's debt of six thousand crowns from the Charter League to 'the Lord of Crowsfoot', with the price left blank; and a printed form of loan at one in ten a month, secured upon the borrower's land, with spaces for name, sum and seal.
inventory.name: Quist's papers
inventory.source: gift: drawn by Quist that evening

inventory.description: A heavy, long-shanked iron key on a fine steel chain, warm from a dead man's throat, its bow cast in the shape of the League's scales.
inventory.name: The factor's key

inventory.description: A heavy iron ring of a dozen house keys of every size, from the coat pegs on the League house landing.
inventory.name: The League house key ring
inventory.source: loot: the coat pegs on the League house landing

inventory.description: The Thornbury house's brass desk seal: the Charter League's scales above the word THORNBURY, on a turned walnut handle, with a stick of the League's green sealing wax. Any paper sealed with it looks like the League's own.
inventory.name: The League's seal
inventory.source: stolen: the factor's desk in the League counting room

inventory.description: A sheaf of a dozen printed League letter-of-credit blanks on heavy watermarked paper, the scales printed at the head, spaces for sum, bearer, house and the factor's hand. Unsigned and unsealed.
inventory.name: Blank League letters of credit
inventory.source: stolen: a locked drawer in the League counting room

inventory.description: A heavy parchment bond under Sir Gerold Ambry's seal and the League's scales: six thousand crowns lent to the castellan of Harrowgate against the revenues of Ditchley and his own estate, interest at one in twenty a quarter, two quarters already in arrears. Whoever holds it can call the debt, or sell it.
inventory.name: Sir Gerold's bond

inventory.description: A fat green-bound register: every League letter of credit drawn on the Thornbury house for five years, by number, sum, date and bearer, with the factor's notes. Your own seven thousand is entered on the last written page.
inventory.name: The League's register of letters

inventory.alias: Bundle of League bonds and deeds
inventory.description: Two chests' worth of papers held as surety, tied in labelled bundles: loans to the miller at Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant's landlord and a dozen Marchwood freeholders, each with the borrower's seal and the sum owed. Together they record a little over four thousand crowns owed to the League by men who live within thirty miles.
inventory.name: Bundle of League bonds and deeds
inventory.note: What's left of the League's Marchwood bonds: three Thornbury wool merchants (300 each) and the Plough and Pennant's landlord (250), all in Thornbury. Settled and handed back: the Aldersons (Day 14) and Oxbow Mill (Day 14). With Hesketh's men: the twelve freeholders' bonds.

inventory.description: Six packets of the factor's correspondence tied in green tape and sealed, some from the League's masters at Gildford, unread.
inventory.name: Sealed League packets

inventory.description: Four green bond-books: the Thornbury house's accounts with every borrower for fifteen years, in the factor's tidy hand.
inventory.name: The League's bond-books

inventory.description: A deed of assignment on the League's own watermarked paper, in Factor Ambrose Leck's precise hand to the life, dated eight days ago and sealed in Thornbury green with the house's brass seal: the Charter League, for value received, assigns to the Lord of Crowsfoot all its right in the bonds of Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant and twelve Marchwood freeholders (schedule attached). A forgery good enough to fool the man who wrote the hand (Ottilie's work: 24).
inventory.name: The League's assignment of bonds
inventory.note: A deed of assignment on the League's own watermarked paper, in Factor Ambrose Leck's precise hand to the life, dated eight days before his death and sealed in Thornbury green with the house's brass seal: the Charter League, for value received, assigns to the Lord of Crowsfoot all its right in the bonds of Oxbow Mill, the Aldersons' moated farm at Brockholt, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant and twelve Marchwood freeholders (schedule attached). A forgery good enough to fool the man who wrote the hand (Ottilie's work: 24).
inventory.source: crafted: Ottilie's forgery at the Crow and Kettle

inventory.description: A Charter League letter of credit for fifteen hundred crowns, payable to bearer at the League's Kingsholt house, in Master Pell's hand under the scales seal.
inventory.name: Pell's letter on Kingsholt (1,500)
inventory.source: reward: Master Pell, for the Thornbury letter

inventory.description: A Charter League letter of credit for one thousand crowns, payable to bearer at the League's Gildford house, in Master Pell's hand under the scales seal.
inventory.name: Pell's second letter on Gildford (1,000)
inventory.source: reward: Master Pell, for the Thornbury letter

inventory.description: A deed of sale in Master Pell's clean hand, witnessed under the League's scales: the coaching inn called Coldharbour on the Gallows track, its walls, stables, yard and rights of way, sold by Joss Moss, innkeeper, to the Lord of Crowsfoot for a League letter of two thousand crowns on Gildford, the vendor to keep his room and bar for life at fifteen crowns a month.
inventory.name: The deed to Coldharbour

inventory.description: Four silver candlesticks, a silver ewer and six silver cups, plain and heavy, a farmer's wife's pride, wrapped in a canvas sack.
inventory.name: Agnes Alderson's silver
inventory.source: reward: Hamon Alderson's bond, settled in kind

inventory.description: A heavy gold signet ring set with a carnelian cut with a boar's head: Hamon Alderson's father's.
inventory.name: The Alderson signet
inventory.source: reward: Hamon Alderson's bond, settled in kind

inventory.description: A brass badge in the shape of the Charter League's scales on a pin, from the shoulder of the League's hired man at Thornbury's West Gate; scorched on one edge. It marks a man the League pays to carry arms.
inventory.name: League man's badge

inventory.description: Lot 9. A masterwork skeleton key of blued steel, its bow shaped like a bird in flight: the Magpie's own. Catalogued as 'removed from exhibit The Thief during routine cleaning.'
inventory.name: The Magpie's Key
inventory.source: stolen: Lot 9, lifted from Dorothea Quill mid-raid

inventory.description: A ready-made gentleman's suit from Faircloth's of Silk Lane: close-cut charcoal worsted coat and waistcoat with dull horn buttons, white shirt, black silk stock, dark trousers, good black boots and a low-crowned black hat. Stylish, quiet, expensive-looking without shining.
inventory.name: Fine clothes (charcoal)
inventory.source: gift: bought by Asche at Faircloth's for 15 gp

inventory.name: Paper
inventory.note: About thirty blank customs clearance forms from before the Council's new quay, kept dry in an oilcloth wrap. Each is headed with the old harbour customs crest and has spaces for vessel, master, cargo, duty paid and the Collector's seal. Good stock for a forger.
inventory.source: found: oilcloth bundle in the clerks' pigeonholes, Old Customs House

inventory.name: Rapier
inventory.note: Valentin Crane's walking cane: black lacquered wood with a silver heron's-head handle. A twist of the handle draws a slim, needle-pointed blade. It passes for a gentleman's cane anywhere a sword would draw looks. The engine treats it as a Rapier.
inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.
inventory.name: Oilcloth wrap

inventory.description: A Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame with a leather strap.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor
Dagger of Venom
inventory.note: Acquisitions exhibit A-148, lifted from its glass case in the Undercroft Stores. A slim blade of blued black steel with a green-enamelled hilt, faintly oily to the touch. A plain dagger lies on the black felt in its place, under an unbroken Acquisitions seal.
inventory.source: stolen: Acquisitions case A-148, Cage Three, Undercroft Stores (swapped for a plain dagger)

inventory.description: The Emissary's pin: a closed eye in black enamel on gold, the twin of Crane's coin. Worth perhaps 50 gp to a jeweller; worth a great deal more to whoever it belonged to.
inventory.name: Black-gold closed-eye pin

inventory.description: A folded letter in a foreign hand on heavy cream paper, sealed in black wax with a closed eye. It names its bearer only as 'the Envoy of the Lidless Court' and asks every harbourmaster of the Obsidian Coast to give him passage and no questions.
inventory.name: Letter of passage (Lidless Court)

inventory.description: Heavy gold coins stamped with a rayed sun on one face and a closed eye on the other. A money-changer would give about 25 gp each.
inventory.name: Foreign gold 'sun' coins

inventory.description: A small black iron key on a silk cord, from round the Emissary's neck. It fits the black lacquer casket.
inventory.name: Casket key on a cord
Mule
inventory.note: The grey mule taken with the cart on the March Road. Its near-hind shoe is cracked, leaving a forked print: it wants a farrier.
inventory.source: stolen: the Rookery's own mule, back from the Hanged Men's horse line

inventory.name: Book
inventory.note: A thumb-sized book bound in greasy calfskin, its pages ruled in columns in a small neat hand, with a stub of pencil tied to the spine. It was under the pillow in the big tent, wrapped in a stocking.
inventory.source: found: under the woman's pillow in the big tent

inventory.description: A letter in a soldier's square hand, from Lucan Mire to Sir Gerold Ambry of Harrowgate, offering his twelve men for the Fallowfield lands and a title. It breaks off mid-sentence.
inventory.name: Lucan's unfinished letter

inventory.description: trinket
inventory.name: Silver eye pendant

inventory.description: an iron eye on a chain, the holy symbol of the Lidless church
inventory.name: Iron eye holy symbol

inventory.description: a dozen letters tied with grey ribbon, several under a seal of an open eye, from Ennis's strongbox (unread)
inventory.name: Bundle of sealed letters

inventory.description: a folded writ under Harrowgate's seal (a tower and a stag), from Sergeant Thorley's belt pouch, singed at one corner (unread)
inventory.name: Sealed orders of Sir Gerold

inventory.description: A long roll of heavy paper in an oiled-leather tube under the Regency's antler seal: the Marchwood's war-tax for the season, village by village, landholder by landholder, what was assessed, what was paid and what is still owed, in a clerk's tight hand. Unread.
inventory.name: The Marchwood tally-roll
inventory.source: loot: the oiled-leather tube strapped inside the tax wagon's tailboard

inventory.description: In Quist's careful hand (a little shakier on the left margins): a bill of sale for the assignment of Sir Gerold Ambry's debt of six thousand crowns from the Charter League to 'the Lord of Crowsfoot', with the price left blank; and a printed form of loan at one in ten a month, secured upon the borrower's land, with spaces for name, sum and seal.
inventory.name: Quist's papers
inventory.source: gift: drawn by Quist that evening

inventory.description: A heavy, long-shanked iron key on a fine steel chain, warm from a dead man's throat, its bow cast in the shape of the League's scales.
inventory.name: The factor's key

inventory.description: A heavy iron ring of a dozen house keys of every size, from the coat pegs on the League house landing.
inventory.name: The League house key ring
inventory.source: loot: the coat pegs on the League house landing

inventory.description: The Thornbury house's brass desk seal: the Charter League's scales above the word THORNBURY, on a turned walnut handle, with a stick of the League's green sealing wax. Any paper sealed with it looks like the League's own.
inventory.name: The League's seal
inventory.source: stolen: the factor's desk in the League counting room

inventory.description: A sheaf of a dozen printed League letter-of-credit blanks on heavy watermarked paper, the scales printed at the head, spaces for sum, bearer, house and the factor's hand. Unsigned and unsealed.
inventory.name: Blank League letters of credit
inventory.source: stolen: a locked drawer in the League counting room

inventory.description: A heavy parchment bond under Sir Gerold Ambry's seal and the League's scales: six thousand crowns lent to the castellan of Harrowgate against the revenues of Ditchley and his own estate, interest at one in twenty a quarter, two quarters already in arrears. Whoever holds it can call the debt, or sell it.
inventory.name: Sir Gerold's bond

inventory.description: A fat green-bound register: every League letter of credit drawn on the Thornbury house for five years, by number, sum, date and bearer, with the factor's notes. Your own seven thousand is entered on the last written page.
inventory.name: The League's register of letters

inventory.alias: Bundle of League bonds and deeds
inventory.description: Two chests' worth of papers held as surety, tied in labelled bundles: loans to the miller at Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant's landlord and a dozen Marchwood freeholders, each with the borrower's seal and the sum owed. Together they record a little over four thousand crowns owed to the League by men who live within thirty miles.
inventory.name: Bundle of League bonds and deeds
inventory.note: What's left of the League's Marchwood bonds: three Thornbury wool merchants (300 each) and the Plough and Pennant's landlord (250), all in Thornbury. Settled and handed back: the Aldersons (Day 14) and Oxbow Mill (Day 14). With Hesketh's men: the twelve freeholders' bonds.

inventory.description: Six packets of the factor's correspondence tied in green tape and sealed, some from the League's masters at Gildford, unread.
inventory.name: Sealed League packets

inventory.description: Four green bond-books: the Thornbury house's accounts with every borrower for fifteen years, in the factor's tidy hand.
inventory.name: The League's bond-books

inventory.description: A deed of assignment on the League's own watermarked paper, in Factor Ambrose Leck's precise hand to the life, dated eight days ago and sealed in Thornbury green with the house's brass seal: the Charter League, for value received, assigns to the Lord of Crowsfoot all its right in the bonds of Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant and twelve Marchwood freeholders (schedule attached). A forgery good enough to fool the man who wrote the hand (Ottilie's work: 24).
inventory.name: The League's assignment of bonds
inventory.note: A deed of assignment on the League's own watermarked paper, in Factor Ambrose Leck's precise hand to the life, dated eight days before his death and sealed in Thornbury green with the house's brass seal: the Charter League, for value received, assigns to the Lord of Crowsfoot all its right in the bonds of Oxbow Mill, the Aldersons' moated farm at Brockholt, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant and twelve Marchwood freeholders (schedule attached). A forgery good enough to fool the man who wrote the hand (Ottilie's work: 24).
inventory.source: crafted: Ottilie's forgery at the Crow and Kettle

inventory.description: A Charter League letter of credit for fifteen hundred crowns, payable to bearer at the League's Kingsholt house, in Master Pell's hand under the scales seal.
inventory.name: Pell's letter on Kingsholt (1,500)
inventory.source: reward: Master Pell, for the Thornbury letter

inventory.description: A Charter League letter of credit for one thousand crowns, payable to bearer at the League's Gildford house, in Master Pell's hand under the scales seal.
inventory.name: Pell's second letter on Gildford (1,000)
inventory.source: reward: Master Pell, for the Thornbury letter

inventory.description: A deed of sale in Master Pell's clean hand, witnessed under the League's scales: the coaching inn called Coldharbour on the Gallows track, its walls, stables, yard and rights of way, sold by Joss Moss, innkeeper, to the Lord of Crowsfoot for a League letter of two thousand crowns on Gildford, the vendor to keep his room and bar for life at fifteen crowns a month.
inventory.name: The deed to Coldharbour

inventory.description: Four silver candlesticks, a silver ewer and six silver cups, plain and heavy, a farmer's wife's pride, wrapped in a canvas sack.
inventory.name: Agnes Alderson's silver
inventory.source: reward: Hamon Alderson's bond, settled in kind

inventory.description: A heavy gold signet ring set with a carnelian cut with a boar's head: Hamon Alderson's father's.
inventory.name: The Alderson signet
inventory.source: reward: Hamon Alderson's bond, settled in kind

inventory.description: A brass badge in the shape of the Charter League's scales on a pin, from the shoulder of the League's hired man at Thornbury's West Gate; scorched on one edge. It marks a man the League pays to carry arms.
inventory.name: League man's badge

inventory.alias: Bundle of League bonds and deeds
inventory.description: Two chests' worth of papers held as surety, tied in labelled bundles: loans to the miller at Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant's landlord and a dozen Marchwood freeholders, each with the borrower's seal and the sum owed. inventory.note: The last of the League's Marchwood bonds: the three Thornbury wool merchants (300 each) and the Plough and Pennant's landlord (250), all to be paid by Thornbury's council as the town's fine on Day 16. inventory.description: Six packets of the factor's correspondence tied in green tape and sealed, some from the League's masters at Gildford, unread.

inventory.description: Four green bond-books: the Thornbury house's accounts with every borrower for fifteen years, in the factor's tidy hand.
inventory.name: The League's bond-books

inventory.description: A deed of assignment on the League's own watermarked paper, in Factor Ambrose Leck's precise hand to the life, dated eight days ago and sealed in Thornbury green with the house's brass seal: the Charter League, for value received, assigns to the Lord of Crowsfoot all its right in the bonds of Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant and twelve Marchwood freeholders (schedule attached). inventory.name: The League's assignment of bonds

inventory.description: Lot 9. A masterwork skeleton key of blued steel, its bow shaped like a bird in flight: the Magpie's own. Catalogued as 'removed from exhibit The Thief during routine cleaning.'
inventory.name: The Magpie's Key
inventory.source: stolen: Lot 9, lifted from Dorothea Quill mid-raid

inventory.description: A ready-made gentleman's suit from Faircloth's of Silk Lane: close-cut charcoal worsted coat and waistcoat with dull horn buttons, white shirt, black silk stock, dark trousers, good black boots and a low-crowned black hat. Stylish, quiet, expensive-looking without shining.
inventory.name: Fine clothes (charcoal)
inventory.source: gift: bought by Asche at Faircloth's for 15 gp

inventory.name: Paper
inventory.note: About thirty blank customs clearance forms from before the Council's new quay, kept dry in an oilcloth wrap. Each is headed with the old harbour customs crest and has spaces for vessel, master, cargo, duty paid and the Collector's seal. Good stock for a forger.
inventory.source: found: oilcloth bundle in the clerks' pigeonholes, Old Customs House

inventory.name: Rapier
inventory.note: Valentin Crane's walking cane: black lacquered wood with a silver heron's-head handle. A twist of the handle draws a slim, needle-pointed blade. It passes for a gentleman's cane anywhere a sword would draw looks. The engine treats it as a Rapier.
inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.
inventory.name: Oilcloth wrap

inventory.description: A Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame with a leather strap.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor
Dagger of Venom
inventory.note: Acquisitions exhibit A-148, lifted from its glass case in the Undercroft Stores. A slim blade of blued black steel with a green-enamelled hilt, faintly oily to the touch. A plain dagger lies on the black felt in its place, under an unbroken Acquisitions seal.
inventory.source: stolen: Acquisitions case A-148, Cage Three, Undercroft Stores (swapped for a plain dagger)

inventory.description: The Emissary's pin: a closed eye in black enamel on gold, the twin of Crane's coin. Worth perhaps 50 gp to a jeweller; worth a great deal more to whoever it belonged to.
inventory.name: Black-gold closed-eye pin

inventory.description: A folded letter in a foreign hand on heavy cream paper, sealed in black wax with a closed eye. It names its bearer only as 'the Envoy of the Lidless Court' and asks every harbourmaster of the Obsidian Coast to give him passage and no questions.
inventory.name: Letter of passage (Lidless Court)

inventory.description: Heavy gold coins stamped with a rayed sun on one face and a closed eye on the other. A money-changer would give about 25 gp each.
inventory.name: Foreign gold 'sun' coins

inventory.description: A small black iron key on a silk cord, from round the Emissary's neck. It fits the black lacquer casket.
inventory.name: Casket key on a cord
Mule
inventory.note: The grey mule taken with the cart on the March Road. Its near-hind shoe is cracked, leaving a forked print: it wants a farrier.
inventory.source: stolen: the Rookery's own mule, back from the Hanged Men's horse line

inventory.name: Book
inventory.note: A thumb-sized book bound in greasy calfskin, its pages ruled in columns in a small neat hand, with a stub of pencil tied to the spine. It was under the pillow in the big tent, wrapped in a stocking.
inventory.source: found: under the woman's pillow in the big tent

inventory.description: A letter in a soldier's square hand, from Lucan Mire to Sir Gerold Ambry of Harrowgate, offering his twelve men for the Fallowfield lands and a title. It breaks off mid-sentence.
inventory.name: Lucan's unfinished letter

inventory.description: trinket
inventory.name: Silver eye pendant

inventory.description: an iron eye on a chain, the holy symbol of the Lidless church
inventory.name: Iron eye holy symbol

inventory.description: a dozen letters tied with grey ribbon, several under a seal of an open eye, from Ennis's strongbox (unread)
inventory.name: Bundle of sealed letters

inventory.description: a folded writ under Harrowgate's seal (a tower and a stag), from Sergeant Thorley's belt pouch, singed at one corner (unread)
inventory.name: Sealed orders of Sir Gerold

inventory.description: A long roll of heavy paper in an oiled-leather tube under the Regency's antler seal: the Marchwood's war-tax for the season, village by village, landholder by landholder, what was assessed, what was paid and what is still owed, in a clerk's tight hand. Unread.
inventory.name: The Marchwood tally-roll
inventory.source: loot: the oiled-leather tube strapped inside the tax wagon's tailboard

inventory.description: In Quist's careful hand (a little shakier on the left margins): a bill of sale for the assignment of Sir Gerold Ambry's debt of six thousand crowns from the Charter League to 'the Lord of Crowsfoot', with the price left blank; and a printed form of loan at one in ten a month, secured upon the borrower's land, with spaces for name, sum and seal.
inventory.name: Quist's papers
inventory.source: gift: drawn by Quist that evening

inventory.description: A heavy, long-shanked iron key on a fine steel chain, warm from a dead man's throat, its bow cast in the shape of the League's scales.
inventory.name: The factor's key

inventory.description: A heavy iron ring of a dozen house keys of every size, from the coat pegs on the League house landing.
inventory.name: The League house key ring
inventory.source: loot: the coat pegs on the League house landing

inventory.description: The Thornbury house's brass desk seal: the Charter League's scales above the word THORNBURY, on a turned walnut handle, with a stick of the League's green sealing wax. Any paper sealed with it looks like the League's own.
inventory.name: The League's seal
inventory.source: stolen: the factor's desk in the League counting room

inventory.description: A sheaf of a dozen printed League letter-of-credit blanks on heavy watermarked paper, the scales printed at the head, spaces for sum, bearer, house and the factor's hand. Unsigned and unsealed.
inventory.name: Blank League letters of credit
inventory.source: stolen: a locked drawer in the League counting room

inventory.description: A heavy parchment bond under Sir Gerold Ambry's seal and the League's scales: six thousand crowns lent to the castellan of Harrowgate against the revenues of Ditchley and his own estate, interest at one in twenty a quarter, two quarters already in arrears. Whoever holds it can call the debt, or sell it.
inventory.name: Sir Gerold's bond

inventory.description: A fat green-bound register: every League letter of credit drawn on the Thornbury house for five years, by number, sum, date and bearer, with the factor's notes. Your own seven thousand is entered on the last written page.
inventory.name: The League's register of letters

inventory.alias: Bundle of League bonds and deeds
inventory.description: Two chests' worth of papers held as surety, tied in labelled bundles: loans to the miller at Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant's landlord and a dozen Marchwood freeholders, each with the borrower's seal and the sum owed. Together they record a little over four thousand crowns owed to the League by men who live within thirty miles.
inventory.name: Bundle of League bonds and deeds
inventory.note: The last of the League's Marchwood bonds: the three Thornbury wool merchants (300 each) and the Plough and Pennant's landlord (250), all to be paid by Thornbury's council as the town's fine on Day 16. Settled already: the Aldersons and Oxbow Mill. With Hesketh's men: the twelve freeholders' bonds.

inventory.description: Six packets of the factor's correspondence tied in green tape and sealed, some from the League's masters at Gildford, unread.
inventory.name: Sealed League packets

inventory.description: Four green bond-books: the Thornbury house's accounts with every borrower for fifteen years, in the factor's tidy hand.
inventory.name: The League's bond-books

inventory.description: A deed of assignment on the League's own watermarked paper, in Factor Ambrose Leck's precise hand to the life, dated eight days ago and sealed in Thornbury green with the house's brass seal: the Charter League, for value received, assigns to the Lord of Crowsfoot all its right in the bonds of Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant and twelve Marchwood freeholders (schedule attached). A forgery good enough to fool the man who wrote the hand (Ottilie's work: 24).
inventory.name: The League's assignment of bonds
inventory.note: A deed of assignment on the League's own watermarked paper, in Factor Ambrose Leck's precise hand to the life, dated eight days before his death and sealed in Thornbury green with the house's brass seal: the Charter League, for value received, assigns to the Lord of Crowsfoot all its right in the bonds of Oxbow Mill, the Aldersons' moated farm at Brockholt, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant and twelve Marchwood freeholders (schedule attached). A forgery good enough to fool the man who wrote the hand (Ottilie's work: 24).
inventory.source: crafted: Ottilie's forgery at the Crow and Kettle

inventory.description: A Charter League letter of credit for fifteen hundred crowns, payable to bearer at the League's Kingsholt house, in Master Pell's hand under the scales seal.
inventory.name: Pell's letter on Kingsholt (1,500)
inventory.source: reward: Master Pell, for the Thornbury letter

inventory.description: A Charter League letter of credit for one thousand crowns, payable to bearer at the League's Gildford house, in Master Pell's hand under the scales seal.
inventory.name: Pell's second letter on Gildford (1,000)
inventory.source: reward: Master Pell, for the Thornbury letter

inventory.description: A deed of sale in Master Pell's clean hand, witnessed under the League's scales: the coaching inn called Coldharbour on the Gallows track, its walls, stables, yard and rights of way, sold by Joss Moss, innkeeper, to the Lord of Crowsfoot for a League letter of two thousand crowns on Gildford, the vendor to keep his room and bar for life at fifteen crowns a month.
inventory.name: The deed to Coldharbour

inventory.description: Four silver candlesticks, a silver ewer and six silver cups, plain and heavy, a farmer's wife's pride, wrapped in a canvas sack.
inventory.name: Agnes Alderson's silver
inventory.source: reward: Hamon Alderson's bond, settled in kind

inventory.description: A heavy gold signet ring set with a carnelian cut with a boar's head: Hamon Alderson's father's.
inventory.name: The Alderson signet
inventory.source: reward: Hamon Alderson's bond, settled in kind

inventory.description: A brass badge in the shape of the Charter League's scales on a pin, from the shoulder of the League's hired man at Thornbury's West Gate; scorched on one edge. It marks a man the League pays to carry arms.
inventory.name: League man's badge

inventory.description: A heavy iron ring of keys from the dead watch-captain's belt: the watch-house, its lock-up and armoury, the East Gate's wicket, and a big old key stamped with Thornbury's tower: the reeve's hall.
inventory.name: Watch-captain Orme's keys

inventory.description: Two iron keys on a cord with a little silver eye: the Chapel of the Unblinking's doors and its strongroom-closet, surrendered by Reeve Ashby.
inventory.name: Keys of the Lidless chapel
inventory.source: gift: Reeve Ashby's surrender of Thornbury

inventory.description: A ring of four iron keys on a greasy string: the postern's big lock, the well-house, and two smaller ones nobody has told you about.
inventory.name: Mattock's keys
inventory.source: loot: Old Mattock's wrist, the well-house at Harrowgate

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.

inventory.description: A Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame with a leather strap.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor
Dagger of Venom
inventory.note: Acquisitions exhibit A-148, lifted from its glass case in the Undercroft Stores. A slim blade of blued black steel with a green-enamelled hilt, faintly oily to the touch. A plain dagger lies on the black felt in its place, under an unbroken Acquisitions seal.

inventory.description: The Emissary's pin: a closed eye in black enamel on gold, the twin of Crane's coin. Worth perhaps 50 gp to a jeweller; worth a great deal more to whoever it belonged to.

inventory.description: A folded letter in a foreign hand on heavy cream paper, sealed in black wax with a closed eye. It names its bearer only as 'the Envoy of the Lidless Court' and asks every harbourmaster of the Obsidian Coast to give him passage and no questions.
inventory.name: Letter of passage (Lidless Court)

inventory.description: Heavy gold coins stamped with a rayed sun on one face and a closed eye on the other. A money-changer would give about 25 gp each.
inventory.name: Foreign gold 'sun' coins

inventory.description: A small black iron key on a silk cord, from round the Emissary's neck. It fits the black lacquer casket.
inventory.name: Casket key on a cord
Mule

inventory.name: Book

inventory.description: A letter in a soldier's square hand, from Lucan Mire to Sir Gerold Ambry of Harrowgate, offering his twelve men for the Fallowfield lands and a title. It breaks off mid-sentence.

inventory.description: trinket
inventory.name: Silver eye pendant

inventory.description: an iron eye on a chain, the holy symbol of the Lidless church
inventory.name: Iron eye holy symbol

inventory.description: a dozen letters tied with grey ribbon, several under a seal of an open eye, from Ennis's strongbox (unread)
inventory.name: Bundle of sealed letters

inventory.description: a folded writ under Harrowgate's seal (a tower and a stag), from Sergeant Thorley's belt pouch, singed at one corner (unread)
inventory.name: Sealed orders of Sir Gerold

inventory.description: A long roll of heavy paper in an oiled-leather tube under the Regency's antler seal: the Marchwood's war-tax for the season, village by village, landholder by landholder, what was assessed, what was paid and what is still owed, in a clerk's tight hand. Unread.

inventory.source: loot: the oiled-leather tube strapped inside the tax wagon's tailboard

inventory.description: In Quist's careful hand (a little shakier on the left margins): a bill of sale for the assignment of Sir Gerold Ambry's debt of six thousand crowns from the Charter League to 'the Lord of Crowsfoot', with the price left blank; and a printed form of loan at one in ten a month, secured upon the borrower's land, with spaces for name, sum and seal.
inventory.name: Quist's papers
inventory.source: gift: drawn by Quist that evening

inventory.description: A heavy, long-shanked iron key on a fine steel chain, warm from a dead man's throat, its bow cast in the shape of the League's scales.

inventory.description: A heavy iron ring of a dozen house keys of every size, from the coat pegs on the League house landing.
inventory.name: The League house key ring
inventory.source: loot: the coat pegs on the League house landing

inventory.description: The Thornbury house's brass desk seal: the Charter League's scales above the word THORNBURY, on a turned walnut handle, with a stick of the League's green sealing wax. Any paper sealed with it looks like the League's own.
inventory.name: The League's seal
inventory.source: stolen: the factor's desk in the League counting room

inventory.description: A sheaf of a dozen printed League letter-of-credit blanks on heavy watermarked paper, the scales printed at the head, spaces for sum, bearer, house and the factor's hand. Unsigned and unsealed.
inventory.name: Blank League letters of credit
inventory.source: stolen: a locked drawer in the League counting room

inventory.description: A fat green-bound register: every League letter of credit drawn on the Thornbury house for five years, by number, sum, date and bearer, with the factor's notes. Your own seven thousand is entered on the last written page.
inventory.name: The League's register of letters

inventory.alias: Bundle of League bonds and deeds
inventory.description: Two chests' worth of papers held as surety, tied in labelled bundles: loans to the miller at Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant's landlord and a dozen Marchwood freeholders, each with the borrower's seal and the sum owed. Together they record a little over four thousand crowns owed to the League by men who live within thirty miles.
inventory.name: Bundle of League bonds and deeds
inventory.note: The last of the League's Marchwood bonds: the three Thornbury wool merchants (300 each) and the Plough and Pennant's landlord (250), all to be paid by Thornbury's council as the town's fine on Day 16. Settled already: the Aldersons and Oxbow Mill. With Hesketh's men: the twelve freeholders' bonds.

inventory.description: Six packets of the factor's correspondence tied in green tape and sealed, some from the League's masters at Gildford, unread.
inventory.name: Sealed League packets

inventory.description: Four green bond-books: the Thornbury house's accounts with every borrower for fifteen years, in the factor's tidy hand.
inventory.name: The League's bond-books

inventory.description: A deed of assignment on the League's own watermarked paper, in Factor Ambrose Leck's precise hand to the life, dated eight days ago and sealed in Thornbury green with the house's brass seal: the Charter League, for value received, assigns to the Lord of Crowsfoot all its right in the bonds of Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant and twelve Marchwood freeholders (schedule attached). inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'

inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

pois.name: The Heartwood
pois.text: The Thornbound's holiest grove: oaks older than the kingdom, ringed with living thorn and watched over by things that are not entirely trees.

pois.name: The Weeping Yew
pois.text: A vast yew in a hollow of the northern Elderwild that weeps red sap like blood. The Thornbound bury their kings' hearts among its roots.

pois.name: The Green Hollow
pois.text: A drowned-dark valley of the eastern Elderwild where the trees grow black and nothing sings: the lair of a green dragon.

pois.name: Ysm-Tharuun
pois.text: A dead city of green stone in the northern Elderwild, choked with roots: towers carved with coiling serpents, a sunken plaza of broken statues, and a stair that goes down into the dark.

pois.name: The Wolf's Tooth
pois.text: A cave mouth in a crag of the Barrow Hills, shaped like a broken fang. Bones at the entrance, and the musk of something big.

pois.name: The Lesser Barrow
pois.text: A second, smaller grey mound deep in the Barrow Hills, with a serpent-carved lintel half buried in bracken. Nobody local will go near it.

pois.name: Witchlight Mere
pois.text: A black mere in the western woods where green lights walk the water at dusk. Drovers go a mile round rather than pass it.

pois.name: The Sunken Road
pois.text: A deep, overgrown holloway east of Ditchley where an old royal road has sunk between its banks. Smugglers' marks cut into the roots.

pois.name: The Gibbet Oak
pois.text: A dead oak at a crossroads south of Brockholt where Harrowgate's justices used to hang thieves. Eleven iron collars still hang in its branches.

pois.name: The Pale Tower
pois.text: A slim white tower with no door at ground level, standing alone on a western hill.

pois.name: Hob's Leap
pois.text: A cleft in a rocky knoll where a stream drops into the dark. Local boys dare each other to the edge.

pois.name: Kingsfell
pois.text: The broken hall of a forgotten royal hunting seat, swallowed by the wood; an antler crown carved over the door.

pois.name: The Hanging Stones
pois.text: A ring of standing stones in the deep wood, each with an iron chain hanging from a hole bored through it.

pois.name: Spiderglen
pois.text: A dark glen strung with webs as thick as rope. Hunters who go in don't come out.

pois.name: The Wardens' Camp
pois.text: A Thornbound warden camp: bark shelters, a sweat-lodge, a lookout platform in an oak.

pois.name: The Old Watch
pois.text: A ruined watchtower on a spur of the Greyspine, older than the Hollowmark.

pois.name: The Downmoot Stones
pois.text: A ring of grey sarsens on the highest down where the shepherds' moot meets at midsummer.

pois.name: The King's Barrow
pois.text: The largest of the down barrows, with a blocked stone passage and a hole where someone has tried to dig in.

pois.name: The Hag's Copse
pois.text: A copse of twisted hornbeams in the Eastwood where the birds go silent.

pois.name: Saint Aldric's Chapel
pois.text: A ruined forest chapel with a cracked bell still hanging in the tree that has grown through its roof.

settlements.name: Elderhaugh
settlements.text: The Thornbound's tree-town: halls and walkways built high in a stand of giant oaks in the heart of the Elderwild, home to a thousand woodfolk and to the Briar Mother's court.

settlements.name: Thornwick
settlements.text: A Thornbound village of turf-roofed longhouses in a clearing ringed with hawthorn.

settlements.name: Yew Hollow
settlements.text: A hidden Thornbound steading among ancient yews; the folk there paint their faces green for the old rites.

pois.name: The Heartwood
pois.text: The Thornbound's holiest grove: oaks older than the kingdom, ringed with living thorn and watched over by things that are not entirely trees.

pois.name: The Weeping Yew
pois.text: A vast yew in a hollow of the northern Elderwild that weeps red sap like blood. The Thornbound bury their kings' hearts among its roots.

pois.name: The Green Hollow
pois.text: A drowned-dark valley of the eastern Elderwild where the trees grow black and nothing sings: the lair of a green dragon.

pois.name: Ysm-Tharuun
pois.text: A dead city of green stone in the northern Elderwild, choked with roots: towers carved with coiling serpents, a sunken plaza of broken statues, and a stair that goes down into the dark.

pois.name: The Wolf's Tooth
pois.text: A cave mouth in a crag of the Barrow Hills, shaped like a broken fang. Bones at the entrance, and the musk of something big.

pois.name: The Lesser Barrow
pois.text: A second, smaller grey mound deep in the Barrow Hills, with a serpent-carved lintel half buried in bracken. Nobody local will go near it.

pois.name: Witchlight Mere
pois.text: A black mere in the western woods where green lights walk the water at dusk. Drovers go a mile round rather than pass it.

pois.name: The Sunken Road
pois.text: A deep, overgrown holloway east of Ditchley where an old royal road has sunk between its banks. Smugglers' marks cut into the roots.

pois.name: The Gibbet Oak
pois.text: A dead oak at a crossroads south of Brockholt where Harrowgate's justices used to hang thieves. Eleven iron collars still hang in its branches.

pois.name: The Pale Tower
pois.text: A slim white tower with no door at ground level, standing alone on a western hill.

pois.name: Hob's Leap
pois.text: A cleft in a rocky knoll where a stream drops into the dark. Local boys dare each other to the edge.

pois.name: Kingsfell
pois.text: The broken hall of a forgotten royal hunting seat, swallowed by the wood; an antler crown carved over the door.

pois.name: The Hanging Stones
pois.text: A ring of standing stones in the deep wood, each with an iron chain hanging from a hole bored through it.

pois.name: Spiderglen
pois.text: A dark glen strung with webs as thick as rope. Hunters who go in don't come out.

pois.name: The Wardens' Camp
pois.text: A Thornbound warden camp: bark shelters, a sweat-lodge, a lookout platform in an oak.

pois.name: The Old Watch
pois.text: A ruined watchtower on a spur of the Greyspine, older than the Hollowmark.

pois.name: The Downmoot Stones
pois.text: A ring of grey sarsens on the highest down where the shepherds' moot meets at midsummer.

pois.name: The King's Barrow
pois.text: The largest of the down barrows, with a blocked stone passage and a hole where someone has tried to dig in.

pois.name: The Hag's Copse
pois.text: A copse of twisted hornbeams in the Eastwood where the birds go silent.

pois.name: Saint Aldric's Chapel
pois.text: A ruined forest chapel with a cracked bell still hanging in the tree that has grown through its roof.

settlements.name: Elderhaugh
settlements.text: The Thornbound's tree-town: halls and walkways built high in a stand of giant oaks in the heart of the Elderwild, home to a thousand woodfolk and to the Briar Mother's court.

settlements.name: Thornwick
settlements.text: A Thornbound village of turf-roofed longhouses in a clearing ringed with hawthorn.

settlements.name: Yew Hollow
settlements.text: A hidden Thornbound steading among ancient yews; the folk there paint their faces green for the old rites.

inventory.description: Lot 9. A masterwork skeleton key of blued steel, its bow shaped like a bird in flight: the Magpie's own. Catalogued as 'removed from exhibit The Thief during routine cleaning.'
inventory.name: The Magpie's Key
inventory.source: stolen: Lot 9, lifted from Dorothea Quill mid-raid

inventory.description: A ready-made gentleman's suit from Faircloth's of Silk Lane: close-cut charcoal worsted coat and waistcoat with dull horn buttons, white shirt, black silk stock, dark trousers, good black boots and a low-crowned black hat. Stylish, quiet, expensive-looking without shining.
inventory.name: Fine clothes (charcoal)
inventory.source: gift: bought by Asche at Faircloth's for 15 gp

inventory.name: Paper
inventory.note: About thirty blank customs clearance forms from before the Council's new quay, kept dry in an oilcloth wrap. Each is headed with the old harbour customs crest and has spaces for vessel, master, cargo, duty paid and the Collector's seal. Good stock for a forger.
inventory.source: found: oilcloth bundle in the clerks' pigeonholes, Old Customs House

inventory.name: Rapier
inventory.note: Valentin Crane's walking cane: black lacquered wood with a silver heron's-head handle. A twist of the handle draws a slim, needle-pointed blade. It passes for a gentleman's cane anywhere a sword would draw looks. The engine treats it as a Rapier.
inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

inventory.description: A yard of tarred oilcloth with drawstrings, sold by Fathom the chandler: wrapped tight around a book, a lantern or a purse, it keeps the contents dry through a swim.
inventory.name: Oilcloth wrap

inventory.description: A Gala visor: smoked glass in a brass frame with a leather strap.
inventory.name: Smoked-glass visor
Dagger of Venom
inventory.note: Acquisitions exhibit A-148, lifted from its glass case in the Undercroft Stores. A slim blade of blued black steel with a green-enamelled hilt, faintly oily to the touch. A plain dagger lies on the black felt in its place, under an unbroken Acquisitions seal.
inventory.source: stolen: Acquisitions case A-148, Cage Three, Undercroft Stores (swapped for a plain dagger)

inventory.description: The Emissary's pin: a closed eye in black enamel on gold, the twin of Crane's coin. Worth perhaps 50 gp to a jeweller; worth a great deal more to whoever it belonged to.
inventory.name: Black-gold closed-eye pin

inventory.description: A folded letter in a foreign hand on heavy cream paper, sealed in black wax with a closed eye. It names its bearer only as 'the Envoy of the Lidless Court' and asks every harbourmaster of the Obsidian Coast to give him passage and no questions.
inventory.name: Letter of passage (Lidless Court)

inventory.description: Heavy gold coins stamped with a rayed sun on one face and a closed eye on the other. A money-changer would give about 25 gp each.
inventory.name: Foreign gold 'sun' coins

inventory.description: A small black iron key on a silk cord, from round the Emissary's neck. It fits the black lacquer casket.
inventory.name: Casket key on a cord
Mule
inventory.note: The grey mule taken with the cart on the March Road. Its near-hind shoe is cracked, leaving a forked print: it wants a farrier.
inventory.source: stolen: the Rookery's own mule, back from the Hanged Men's horse line

inventory.name: Book
inventory.note: A thumb-sized book bound in greasy calfskin, its pages ruled in columns in a small neat hand, with a stub of pencil tied to the spine. It was under the pillow in the big tent, wrapped in a stocking.
inventory.source: found: under the woman's pillow in the big tent

inventory.description: A letter in a soldier's square hand, from Lucan Mire to Sir Gerold Ambry of Harrowgate, offering his twelve men for the Fallowfield lands and a title. It breaks off mid-sentence.
inventory.name: Lucan's unfinished letter

inventory.description: trinket
inventory.name: Silver eye pendant

inventory.description: an iron eye on a chain, the holy symbol of the Lidless church
inventory.name: Iron eye holy symbol

inventory.description: a dozen letters tied with grey ribbon, several under a seal of an open eye, from Ennis's strongbox (unread)
inventory.name: Bundle of sealed letters

inventory.description: a folded writ under Harrowgate's seal (a tower and a stag), from Sergeant Thorley's belt pouch, singed at one corner (unread)
inventory.name: Sealed orders of Sir Gerold

inventory.description: A long roll of heavy paper in an oiled-leather tube under the Regency's antler seal: the Marchwood's war-tax for the season, village by village, landholder by landholder, what was assessed, what was paid and what is still owed, in a clerk's tight hand. Unread.
inventory.name: The Marchwood tally-roll
inventory.source: loot: the oiled-leather tube strapped inside the tax wagon's tailboard

inventory.description: In Quist's careful hand (a little shakier on the left margins): a bill of sale for the assignment of Sir Gerold Ambry's debt of six thousand crowns from the Charter League to 'the Lord of Crowsfoot', with the price left blank; and a printed form of loan at one in ten a month, secured upon the borrower's land, with spaces for name, sum and seal.
inventory.name: Quist's papers
inventory.source: gift: drawn by Quist that evening

inventory.description: A heavy, long-shanked iron key on a fine steel chain, warm from a dead man's throat, its bow cast in the shape of the League's scales.
inventory.name: The factor's key

inventory.description: The Thornbury house's brass desk seal: the Charter League's scales above the word THORNBURY, on a turned walnut handle, with a stick of the League's green sealing wax. Any paper sealed with it looks like the League's own.
inventory.name: The League's seal
inventory.source: stolen: the factor's desk in the League counting room

inventory.description: A sheaf of a dozen printed League letter-of-credit blanks on heavy watermarked paper, the scales printed at the head, spaces for sum, bearer, house and the factor's hand. Unsigned and unsealed.
inventory.name: Blank League letters of credit
inventory.source: stolen: a locked drawer in the League counting room

inventory.description: A fat green-bound register: every League letter of credit drawn on the Thornbury house for five years, by number, sum, date and bearer, with the factor's notes. Your own seven thousand is entered on the last written page.
inventory.name: The League's register of letters

inventory.alias: Bundle of League bonds and deeds
inventory.description: Two chests' worth of papers held as surety, tied in labelled bundles: loans to the miller at Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant's landlord and a dozen Marchwood freeholders, each with the borrower's seal and the sum owed. Together they record a little over four thousand crowns owed to the League by men who live within thirty miles.
inventory.name: Bundle of League bonds and deeds
inventory.note: The last of the League's Marchwood bonds: the three Thornbury wool merchants (300 each) and the Plough and Pennant's landlord (250), all to be paid by Thornbury's council as the town's fine on Day 16. Settled already: the Aldersons and Oxbow Mill. With Hesketh's men: the twelve freeholders' bonds.

inventory.description: Six packets of the factor's correspondence tied in green tape and sealed, some from the League's masters at Gildford, unread.
inventory.name: Sealed League packets

inventory.description: Four green bond-books: the Thornbury house's accounts with every borrower for fifteen years, in the factor's tidy hand.
inventory.name: The League's bond-books

inventory.description: A deed of assignment on the League's own watermarked paper, in Factor Ambrose Leck's precise hand to the life, dated eight days ago and sealed in Thornbury green with the house's brass seal: the Charter League, for value received, assigns to the Lord of Crowsfoot all its right in the bonds of Oxbow Mill, the moated farm on the Ashpole road, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant and twelve Marchwood freeholders (schedule attached). A forgery good enough to fool the man who wrote the hand (Ottilie's work: 24).
inventory.name: The League's assignment of bonds
inventory.note: A deed of assignment on the League's own watermarked paper, in Factor Ambrose Leck's precise hand to the life, dated eight days before his death and sealed in Thornbury green with the house's brass seal: the Charter League, for value received, assigns to the Lord of Crowsfoot all its right in the bonds of Oxbow Mill, the Aldersons' moated farm at Brockholt, three Thornbury wool merchants, the Plough and Pennant and twelve Marchwood freeholders (schedule attached). inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex
